dervis-irab:93-97.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُبَوَّأَ صِدْقٍ): a noun of place, i.e. a place of truth; the meaning is: We settled them in a praiseworthy abode. It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun).
(الامتراء): seeking doubt despite the evidence being manifest. It is from مرى الضرع, i.e. stroking the udder so that it yields milk.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ بَوَّأْنا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ مُبَوَّأَ صِدْقٍ): the wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), brought to set out the blessings that Allah poured upon the Children of Israel after delivering them. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath, قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq), بوأنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), بني إسرائيل is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and مبوأ صدق is the second object of بوّأ, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) if مبوأ is a maṣdar. (وَرَزَقْناهُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّباتِ فَمَا اخْتَلَفُوا حَتَّى جاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ): ورزقناهم is conjoined to بوأنا; it is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi. من الطيبات is attached to (mutaʿalliq) رزقناهم. فما: the fāʿ is a conjunction and ما is negating; اختلفوا is a verb and its fāʿil; حتى is a particle of limit and of the genitive; جاءهم العلم is a verb, a mafʿūl bihi and a fāʿil. What is meant by the disagreement is the doubts that beset them after the coming of the Messenger Muḥammad ﷺ and the mutual support of his miracles. (إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَقْضِي بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ فِيما كانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ): إنّ and its noun; the clause يقضي is its khabar (predicate); بينهم is attached to يقضي; يوم القيامة is an adverb (ẓarf) also attached to يقضي; فيما is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "deciding concerning what…"; the clause كانوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما; كان and the wāw is its noun; فيه is attached to يختلفون, and the clause يختلفون is the khabar of كانوا. (فَإِنْ كُنْتَ فِي شَكٍّ مِمَّا أَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ): the fāʿ is resumptive, إن is conditional, كنت is كان and its noun, and the verb is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); في شك is its khabar; مما is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of شك, and the clause أنزلنا إليك is the ṣila of ما. (فَسْئَلِ الَّذِينَ يَقْرَؤُنَ الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ): the fāʿ is the linking fāʿ (rābiṭa), اسأل is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is "you", الذين is a mafʿūl bihi, the clause يقرءون الكتاب is the ṣila, and من قبلك is a ḥāl. (لَقَدْ جاءَكَ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ فَلا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ المُمْتَرِينَ): the lām paves the way for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa), قد is a particle of affirmation, جاءك الحق is a verb, a mafʿūl bihi and a fāʿil, and من ربك is attached to جاءك. The fāʿ is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, and تكونن is jussive by لا in position, because it is indeclinable (mabnī); its noun is latent (mustatir), implied as "you", and من الممترين is its khabar. (وَلا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ): its i'rab has already been given. (فَتَكُونَ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ): the fāʿ is causal (sababiyya), and تكون is a defective imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the causal fāʿ; من الخاسرين is its khabar. What the scholars said about this verse will come in the section of Benefits. (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ حَقَّتْ عَلَيْهِمْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ): إنّ and its noun; the clause حقت is the ṣila; عليهم is attached to حقت; كلمة is the fāʿil and ربك is in genitive construct (muḍāf ilayhi) to كلمة; the clause لا يؤمنون is the khabar of إنّ. (وَلَوْ جاءَتْهُمْ كُلُّ آيَةٍ حَتَّى يَرَوُا الْعَذابَ الْأَلِيمَ): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), لو is conditional, جاءتهم كل آية [verb, object and] fāʿil; حتى marks the limit of the negation, يروا is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after حتى, the wāw is the fāʿil, and العذاب is a mafʿūl bihi. The seeing is ocular, and therefore it takes only one object. الأليم is a naʿt. The apodosis (jawāb) of لو is omitted, i.e. "their faith would not then benefit them, just as it did not benefit Pharaoh."

* Benefits:
Al-Zajjāj said: People have asked about this verse a great deal and plunged into it, and there is in the sūra what shows its explanation. For Allah, Glorified is He, addresses the Prophet, and that address includes all creation; so the meaning is: "If you (plural) are in doubt, then ask." The proof of this is His saying at the end of the sūra: «يا أيها الناس إن كنتم في شك من ديني فلا أعبد الذين تعبدون من دون الله ولكن أعبد الله الذي يتوفاكم» (the verse). Thus Allah, Glorified is He, made known that His Prophet is not in doubt. Similar to this is His saying «يا أيها النبي إذا طلقتم النساء», where He said طلقتم (plural) while the address is to the Prophet ﷺ alone. Abū ʿAmr Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Zāhid said: I heard the two imams Thaʿlab and al-Mubarrad say: the meaning of فإن كنت في شك is: "Say, O Muḥammad, to the disbeliever: if you are in doubt…" [Translator's note: the text reads «أبو عمرو ومحمد بن عبد الواحد», with a conjunction; this is evidently one person, Abū ʿUmar Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Zāhid (Ghulām Thaʿlab).]
Al-Farrāʾ said: The address is to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ even though he did not doubt, and Allah knew that he was not doubting; rather, the speech takes the form of affirmation and making understood, just as a son says to his father: "If you are my father, then be kind to me," or [a father] to his son: "If you are my son, then obey me," intending thereby emphasis. Sometimes in emphasis they go as far as the impossible, as in their saying: "The sky wept for the death of so-and-so," i.e. if the sky wept for a dead person it would have wept for him. Likewise here the meaning is: if you were one who doubts and you doubted, then ask those who read the Book before you.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: The matter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is written with them in the Torah and the Gospel, and they recognise him as they recognise their own sons. So He wished to confirm their knowledge of the truth of the Qur'an and of the proof of Muḥammad's prophethood (peace be upon him) and to be emphatic about it, and so He said: "If a doubt should befall you, by way of supposition and hypothesis — and the way of one into whom a doubt about religion has crept is to hasten to resolve it and remove it, either by returning to the rules of religion and its proofs, or by striking ideas against the scholars who alert to the truth — then ask the scholars of the People of the Book."
Abū Ḥayyān said: "What I say is that conditional إن requires the suspension of one thing upon another, and does not entail that its occurrence is certain or even possible; rather, that may be in what is rationally impossible, as in His saying, Exalted is He: «قل إن كان للرحمن ولد فأنا أول العابدين» — and it is impossible that He should have a son — and likewise this: it is impossible that he should be in doubt. And it may be in what is impossible by custom, as in His saying: «فإن استطعت أن تبتغي نفقا في الأرض أو سلما في السماء فتأتيهم بآية», i.e. then do so. But the occurrence of إن for suspension upon the impossible is rare, and this verse is of that kind. Since this aspect was hidden from most people, they differed over how to explain this verse."

dervis-irab:98-100.t:
* I'rab:
(فَلَوْلا كانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ آمَنَتْ): the fāʿ is resumptive and لولا is for urging (taḥḍīḍ); this urging carries the sense of rebuke and negation. Reference has already been made to the particles of urging. كانت قرية is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), because كان here is complete (tāmma), and the clause آمنت is a naʿt (adjective) of قرية. (فَنَفَعَها إِيمانُها إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ): the fāʿ is a conjunction and نفعها is conjoined to the naʿt, conjoining the effect to the cause; إيمانها is the fāʿil of نفعها; the clause may stand in place of a naʿt of an indefinite noun. إلا قوم يونس is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil) falling on the meaning, not on the outward wording, as though He said: "Why did the people of a town not believe?" — all of them sharing in the punishment, and the people of Yūnus being excepted from all. Like this exception is His saying, Exalted is He: «فلولا كان من القرون من قبلكم أولو بقية ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض إلا قليلا ممن أنجينا منهم». Al-Zajjāj said that إلا قوم يونس is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), its implied form being "but the people of Yūnus, when they believed…", and like it is the saying of al-Nābigha:
وقفت فيها أصيلا كي اسائلها ... عيّت جوابا وما بالربع من أحد
إلا الأواري لأيا ما أبيّنها ... والنؤي كالحوض بالمظلومة الجلد
(I stopped there at late afternoon to question it; it was unable to answer, and there was no one in the encampment — except the tethering-posts, which I could barely make out, and the trench around the tent, like a cistern in hard, untouched ground.)
يونس is a muḍāf ilayhi, a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) because it is a proper name and foreign. (لَمَّا آمَنُوا كَشَفْنا عَنْهُمْ عَذابَ الْخِزْيِ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وَمَتَّعْناهُمْ إِلى حِينٍ): لما is temporal (ḥīniyya) or linking, آمنوا is a verb and its fāʿil, the clause كشفنا has no grammatical position, عنهم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) كشفنا, عذاب الخزي is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), في الحياة is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), الدنيا is a naʿt, متعناهم is conjoined to كشفنا, and إلى حين is attached to متعناهم. (وَلَوْ شاءَ رَبُّكَ لَآمَنَ مَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ كُلُّهُمْ جَمِيعاً): the wāw is resumptive, لو is conditional, شاء ربك is a verb and its fāʿil; لآمن: the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو, and the clause آمن has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. من is the fāʿil of آمن, في الأرض is the ṣila (relative clause) of من, كلهم is a tawkīd (emphasis) of من, and جميعا is accusative as a ḥāl from «من». (أَفَأَنْتَ تُكْرِهُ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ): the hamza is interrogative and the fāʿ is a conjunction; أنت is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause after it is the khabar (predicate). We have already seen that either the hamza is placed before the conjunction, or there is an omitted clause. حتى is a particle of cause and of the genitive, يكونوا is accusative by an implied أن after حتى, and مؤمنين is the khabar of يكونوا. (وَما كانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): the wāw is a conjunction, ما is negating, كان is a defective past verb, لنفس is its fronted khabar, and the maṣdar-forming أن together with what is in its domain is its postponed noun; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and بإذن الله is attached to تؤمن. (وَيَجْعَلُ الرِّجْسَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ لا يَعْقِلُونَ): ويجعل is conjoined to something implied, as though it were said: "So He gives leave to some of them to believe, and He places…". يجعل is an imperfect verb, الرجس is its object, على الذين is attached to يجعل, and the clause لا يعقلون is the ṣila.

dervis-irab:101-103.t:
* Vocabulary:
(النظر): seeking a thing by way of thought, just as one seeks to perceive it with the eye; the meaning is: reflect with the reflection of one who takes heed.
(النُّذُرُ): plural of نذير, the one who brings warning.

* I'rab:
(قُلِ انْظُرُوا ماذا فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): قل is an imperative verb, and the clause انظروا is the speech reported by "say" (maqūl al-qawl). As for ماذا, it may be that ما is interrogative, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and ذا is a relative noun, the khabar (predicate); the clause is then in the position of the accusative, because the governing word, انظروا, is suspended (taʿlīq) from it by the interrogative. It may also be that ماذا as a whole is an interrogative in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and في السموات is its khabar. On the first view the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element which is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, i.e. "what is it that is established in the heavens and the earth". (وَما تُغْنِي الْآياتُ وَالنُّذُرُ عَنْ قَوْمٍ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ): this clause is either a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in انظروا, as though it were said: "Look, while the fact is that looking does not benefit you," or it is parenthetical (muʿtariḍa). ما is negating, or interrogative in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of تغني, i.e. "what avail do they avail?"; الآيات is the fāʿil (agent), النذر is conjoined to الآيات, عن قوم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تغني, and the clause لا يؤمنون is a naʿt (adjective) of قوم. (فَهَلْ يَنْتَظِرُونَ إِلَّا مِثْلَ أَيَّامِ الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): the fāʿ is resumptive, هل is an interrogative particle, ينتظرون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), مثل is the object of ينتظرون, أيام is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), الذين is in genitive construct to أيام, the clause خلوا is the ṣila, and من قبلهم is attached to خلوا or to an omitted ḥāl. (قُلْ فَانْتَظِرُوا إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمُنْتَظِرِينَ): قل is an imperative verb, the fāʿ is the faṣīḥa fāʿ (the fāʿ implying an omitted condition), انتظروا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; إنّ and its noun, من المنتظرين is its khabar, and the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to an omitted ḥāl.
(ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي رُسُلَنا وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay, ننجي is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), implied as "We", and the clause is conjoined to omitted speech, its implied form being "We destroy the nations, then We save Our messengers", by way of narrating past states. رسلنا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), الذين is conjoined to رسلنا, and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila. (كَذلِكَ حَقًّا عَلَيْنا نُنْجِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a saving like that saving", so it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, and what governs it is ننجي المؤمنين. You may also make the kāf in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, which they have implied as "the matter is thus". حقا is accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. "it is truly due, truly"; it may also be parsed as accusative as a ḥāl, even though its form is that of a maṣdar. Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm, the blind grammarian, put forward a novel view, namely that it is accusative as a badal (substitute) from كذلك. علينا is attached to حقا, ننجي is an imperfect verb, and المؤمنين is a mafʿūl bihi.

* Rhetoric:
The representational simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī) in His saying كذلك ننجي etc.: He likened the salvation of the believers who remain to the salvation of those who have passed, in that it is binding for them and a right due upon Allah. The point of resemblance is that each of them merits salvation.

dervis-irab:104-109.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِنْ دِينِي): قل is an imperative verb; يا أيها الناس has been parsed many times before; إن is conditional, كنتم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), being كان and its noun, في شك is its khabar (predicate), and من ديني is a naʿt (adjective) of شك. (فَلا أَعْبُدُ الَّذِينَ تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ): the fāʿ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), لا is negating, أعبد is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is "I", الذين is the object of أعبد, the clause تعبدون is the ṣila (relative clause), and من دون الله is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَلكِنْ أَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ الَّذِي يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk) without governing effect, أعبد is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is "I", the Name of Majesty is its object, الذي is a naʿt, and the clause يتوفاكم is the ṣila. (وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction, أمرت is a passive past verb and the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); أن with what is in its domain is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "to be" (بأن أكون), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) أمرت; the noun of أكون is latent (mustatir), implied as "I", and من المؤمنين is the khabar of أكون. (وَأَنْ أَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفاً): the wāw is a conjunction, and أن with what is in its domain is conjoined to what precedes it, as though it were said: "and it was said to me: 'and set…'". But the parsing of the maṣdar (verbal noun) is problematic, since conjoining it to أن أكون presents a difficulty, because conjoining a performative (inshāʾ) to a declarative (khabar) is not allowed. However, Sībawayh permitted أن to be connected to an imperative or a prohibition, and compared that to their saying أنت الذي تفعل with second-person address, because the purpose is to connect it with something with which it has the meaning of a maṣdar, and the imperative and the prohibition indicate the maṣdar just as other verbs do. Al-Bayḍāwī summarised what Sībawayh expounded at length; he said: "وأن أقم is conjoined to أن أكون, except that the ṣila of أن is reported in the imperative form, and there is no harm in that, because the basis for allowing it to be connected to the forms of all verbs is their indicating the maṣdar, and that does not differ between declarative and requestive. The requirement that the ṣila be declarative for the nominal relative is only in order to arrive at describing definite nouns by clauses, and they are described only by declarative clauses; the particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) is not like that." [Translator's note: the source prints «الموصول الحر في», a split of «الحرفي».] This is also a summary of what al-Zamakhsharī said, and Abū al-Suʿūd followed it. Others, however, chose that the maṣdar-forming «أن» with what is in its domain is in the position of the nominative through an implied verb, i.e. "and it was said to me" — and we do not hold this view. As for al-Samīn Shihāb al-Dīn al-Ḥalabī, he said, verbatim: "His saying وأن أقم may be on the implication of a verb, i.e. 'and it was revealed to me: set…'. Then you have two views concerning أن: first, that it is explicative (tafsīriyya) of that implied clause — and this is questionable, since what is explained may not be omitted; second, that it is maṣdar-forming, so that it together with what is in its domain is in the position of the nominative by that implied verb."
أقم is an imperative verb, وجهك is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), للدين is attached to أقم, and حنيفا is a ḥāl from الدين or from الوجه. (وَلا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, تكونن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) because it is attached to the nūn of emphasis, in the position of the jussive by لا; the noun of تكونن is latent, implied as "you", and من المشركين is its khabar.
(وَلا تَدْعُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لا يَنْفَعُكَ وَلا يَضُرُّكَ): the wāw is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, تدع is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا, and the fāʿil is "you"; من دون الله is a ḥāl, ما is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi, the clause لا ينفعك is the ṣila, and the clause ولا يضرك is conjoined to لا ينفعك.
(فَإِنْ فَعَلْتَ فَإِنَّكَ إِذاً مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ): the fāʿ is a conjunction, إن is conditional, فعلت is in the position of the jussive as the protasis, the fāʿ is linking (rābiṭa), إنّ and its noun, إذن is a particle of answer and requital, without governing effect (muhmal), and من الظالمين is the khabar of إنّ. (وَإِنْ يَمْسَسْكَ اللَّهُ بِضُرٍّ فَلا كاشِفَ لَهُ إِلَّا هُوَ): the wāw is a conjunction, إن is conditional, يمسسك is the protasis, the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi, الله is the fāʿil, بضر is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يمسسك; the fāʿ is linking, لا is the lā of generic negation, كاشف is its noun, indeclinable on the fatḥa, له is attached to كاشف, and the khabar is omitted. It may also be that له is the khabar, i.e. "existing for it". إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and هو is a badal (substitute) from the omitted khabar, as was set out before concerning «لا إله إلا الله».
(وَإِنْ يُرِدْكَ بِخَيْرٍ فَلا رَادَّ لِفَضْلِهِ): the wāw is a conjunction, إن is conditional, يردك is the protasis, jussive, the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi, بخير is attached to يردك; the fāʿ is linking, لا is the lā of generic negation, راد is its noun, لفضله is attached to راد, and the khabar is omitted; it may also be that the preposition and its genitive noun is the khabar, as set out before. (يُصِيبُ بِهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ مِنْ عِبادِهِ وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ): the clause يصيب is resumptive and the fāʿil is "He"; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يصيب, من is the object of يصيب, the clause يشاء is the ṣila, and من عباده is a ḥāl. وهو: the wāw is resumptive, هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject), الغفور is a first khabar and الرحيم a second khabar. (قُلْ يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ قَدْ جاءَكُمُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ): قد جاءكم الحق is a verb, a mafʿūl bihi and a fāʿil, and من ربكم is attached to جاءكم.
(فَمَنِ اهْتَدى فَإِنَّما يَهْتَدِي لِنَفْسِهِ): the fāʿ is the faṣīḥa fāʿ, من is conditional or relative, a mubtadaʾ, اهتدى is the protasis [or] the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun; the fāʿ is linking, إنما is the restraining [ما] and the restrained [إنّ] (kāffa wa-makfūfa), يهتدي is an imperfect verb with the fāʿil "he", and لنفسه is attached to يهتدي. (وَمَنْ ضَلَّ فَإِنَّما يَضِلُّ عَلَيْها): the parsing of its like has already been given.
(وَما أَنَا عَلَيْكُمْ بِوَكِيلٍ): the wāw is resumptive, ما is the Ḥijāzī negating ما, أنا is its noun, عليكم is attached to وكيل, and وكيل is the khabar of the Ḥijāzī ما in position. (وَاتَّبِعْ ما يُوحى إِلَيْكَ): the wāw is resumptive, because conjoining a performative to a declarative is considered unlikely; اتبع is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is "you", ما is a mafʿūl bihi, the clause يوحى is the ṣila, and إليك is attached to يوحى. (وَاصْبِرْ حَتَّى يَحْكُمَ اللَّهُ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الْحاكِمِينَ): اصبر is an imperative verb conjoined to اتبع, حتى is a particle of limit and of the genitive, يحكم is accusative by an implied أن after حتى and الله is its fāʿil; وهو: the wāw is resumptive, هو is a mubtadaʾ and خير الحاكمين is its khabar.

dervis-irab:1-4.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الر): this has been discussed in detail before, so renew your acquaintance with it.
(الآية): the sign that indicates the end of a stretch of speech from a particular aspect.
(الْحَكِيمِ): here in the sense of المُحكَم (made firm, decisive): faʿīl in the sense of mufʿal. Al-Aʿshā said:
وغريبة تأتي الملوك حكيمة ... قد قلتها ليقال: من ذا قالها؟
(Many a rare, well-made [ode] that comes to kings I have composed, so that it be asked: who is it that composed it?)
It is also said that الحكيم is in the sense of الحاكم (the one who judges), the evidence for which is the saying of Allah the Exalted «ليحكم بين الناس فيما اختلفوا فيه». Discussion of wisdom (al-ḥikma) and its prevalence in the Qur'an will come in the section on Benefits.
(قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ): القَدَم, with two fatḥas, is the thing you send ahead of you so that it is a provision for you until you come to it. Abū ʿUbayda and al-Kisāʾī said: every precedence in good or evil is, among the Arabs, a قَدَم, and it is feminine; one says قدم حسنة. Ḥassān ibn Thābit said:
لنا القدم العليا إليك وخلفنا ... لأولنا في طاعة الله تابع
(Ours is the highest precedence with you, and behind us, following our first ones in obedience to Allah, is a follower.)
And Dhū al-Rumma said:
لكم قدم لا ينكر الناس أنها ... مع الحسب العادي طمت على البحر
(Yours is a precedence which people do not deny, that, together with ancient nobility, it overflowed the sea.)
More discussion of it will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(القسط): justice; it is with kasra on the qāf (القِسط), and from it comes القِسط in the sense of a share. القَسط, with fatḥa on the qāf, is injustice, and القَسَط is a crookedness in the legs.
(الحميم): water heated by fire to the utmost heating. Al-Muraqqish al-Aṣghar said:
في كل يوم لها مقطّرة ... فيها كباء معد وحميم
(Every day she has a censer in which there is prepared aloes-wood incense, and hot water.)

* I'rab:
(الر، تِلْكَ آياتُ الْكِتابِ الْحَكِيمِ): the i'rab of (الر) was given in Sūrat al-Baqara, so renew your acquaintance with it. (تلك) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (آيات الكتاب) is the khabar (predicate), and (الحكيم) is a naʿt (adjective) of (الكتاب). (أَكانَ لِلنَّاسِ عَجَباً أَنْ أَوْحَيْنا إِلى رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (istifhām inkārī) mixed with wonder; (كان) is a deficient past verb; (للناس) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it precedes the adjective [i.e. what would have been its qualified noun]; (عجبا) is the fronted khabar of (كان); (أن أوحينا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of nominative as the noun of (كان); (إلى رجل) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أوحينا); and (منهم) is a naʿt of (رجل). (أَنْ أَنْذِرِ النَّاسَ): (أن) is explicative (mufassira) — the one that occurs after a clause containing the meaning of saying without its letters — or it is lightened from the heavy (أنّ), its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause (أنذر الناس) is the object of an omitted saying which is in the position of nominative as the khabar of (أنّ), in the sense that "the matter is Our saying: warn the people".
(وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنَّ لَهُمْ قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ): (وبشر) is conjoined to (أنذر); (الذين) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila (relative clause). (أنّ) is a particle resembling the verb, and it with what falls under it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "with that…" (بأن); (لهم) is its fronted khabar and (قدم صدق) its postponed noun; the adverb (عند ربهم) is attached to an omitted naʿt of (قدم صدق). (قالَ الْكافِرُونَ: إِنَّ هذا لَساحِرٌ مُبِينٌ): the clause is resumptive, as though it were asked: what did they do after the wonder? (قال الكافرون) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (إنّ), its noun and its khabar, with the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (مبين) is a naʿt of (ساحر); and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ): (إنّ), its noun and its khabar; (الذي) is a naʿt of (الله); the clause (خلق السموات والأرض) is the ṣila; and (في ستة أيام) is attached to (خلق). (ثُمَّ اسْتَوى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ): (ثم) is a conjunction of delay; (استوى) is conjoined to (خلق); (على العرش) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (استوى). The clause (يدبر الأمر) is a second khabar of (إنّ); it may also be a ḥāl, or resumptive with no grammatical position. (ما مِنْ شَفِيعٍ إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ إِذْنِهِ): (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative (mā al-ḥijāziyya); (من) is redundant (zāʾida); (شفيع) is genitive in form and the noun of (ما) in position; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (من بعد إذنه) is attached to an omitted khabar. (ذلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ أَفَلا تَذَكَّرُونَ): (ذلكم) is a mubtadaʾ, (الله) is a badal (substitute), and (ربكم) is the khabar of (ذلكم). The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; (اعبدوه) is an imperative verb, its agent and a direct object. The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval, intended to urge reflection and remembrance; the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to something omitted; (لا) is negative; and (تذكرون) is an imperfect verb, originally (تتذكرون). (إِلَيْهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعاً): (إليه) is a fronted khabar and (مرجعكم) a postponed mubtadaʾ; (جميعا) is accusative as a ḥāl. (وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا): (وعد الله) is accusative as a maṣdar, because His saying (إليه مرجعكم) means the promise of return; (حقا) is accusative as a maṣdar, its implied form being "that is due, a being-due". (إِنَّهُ يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ): (إنّ) and its noun, and the clause (يبدأ) is its khabar; (الخلق) is a direct object; (ثم يعيده) is conjoined to (يبدأ الخلق). The clause is resumptive, brought to give the reason for the existence of creation and their return to Him. (لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ بِالْقِسْطِ): the lām is causal; (يجزي) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied (أن); (الذين) is the object of (يجزي); the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; (وعملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to (آمنوا); (بالقسط) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يجزي), i.e. because of their equity and justice. It may also be a ḥāl, either from the agent or from the object, i.e. He recompenses them in a state bound up with equity, that is, being just; or [them] being bound up with it. (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَهُمْ شَرابٌ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ وَعَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ بِما كانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ): (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila; (لهم) is a fronted khabar and (شراب) a postponed mubtadaʾ; (من حميم) is a naʿt of (شراب); (عذاب) is conjoined to (شراب); the clause (لهم شراب) is the khabar of (الذين); and (أليم) is a naʿt of (عذاب). In (بما), the bāʾ is a causal genitive particle and (ما) is maṣdar-forming; (كانوا) is (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يكفرون) is its khabar, i.e. because of their unbelief. The preposition and its genitive noun are a second naʿt of (عذاب); it may also be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. that is because of their unbelief.

* Rhetoric:
1- The loose metonymic trope (al-majāz al-mursal) in His saying: «أن لهم قدم صدق». The word "foot" (القدم) is applied to striving and precedence, because these are attained only by the foot; so the effect is named by the name of the cause, just as a favour is called a "hand" because it is given by the hand. The relation here is causality; it has been discussed before. We add here that the trope is not regular (muṭṭarid), so it is not correct to say قدم سوء. This is a remarkable property of tropes, the judgement in which almost goes back to taste.
2- The verbal correspondence (munāsaba lafẓiyya) between حميم and أليم. Correspondence is of two kinds: correspondence in meanings and correspondence in words. Correspondence of meaning was mentioned in al-Anʿām. Here the correspondence is verbal: it consists in bringing words of matching measure, rhymed or unrhymed, so it is complete or incomplete. The incomplete kind occurs more in eloquent speech, because rhyming is not required in it.

* Benefits:
1- Wisdom (al-ḥikma) in the Qur'an:
The word ḥikma is widespread in the Qur'an, and the Qur'an is described as wise (al-ḥakīm); much of that has passed with us and more of it will pass. We shall find the word "the Book" coupled with the word "wisdom", the latter conjoined to it. Allah the Exalted said: «وأنزل الله عليك الكتاب والحكمة». Professor Muṣṭafā ʿAbd al-Rāziq holds in his studies on Islamic philosophy: "It is possible that the word ḥikma in the Arabic language is synonymous with the Greek word 'philosophy', and tracing this word guides us to the origin of distinguished thought among the Arabs. The word existed in the Jāhiliyya, and the evidences for it are very many. The meaning of ḥikma in the Qur'an is, in most instances, the Sunna of the Prophet, and there is no disagreement in establishing this meaning. The linguists said: ḥikma and ḥukm are from one root. Some orientalists hold that the word is Hebrew and that its meaning in that language is judgement, i.e. also ḥukm. Ḥikma in its general meaning indicates soundness and mastery of opinion and action; Allah the Exalted said: «ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا»." This statement is sound to a great extent, and Imam al-Shāfiʿī preceded [him] in establishing something of this, for he said: "What is meant by ḥikma is the Sunna of the Prophet ﷺ."
2- Annexing the qualified noun to the adjective and vice versa: the base rule is that a qualified noun is not annexed to its adjective, as in رجل فاضل, and an adjective is not annexed to its qualified noun, as in فاضل رجل. What occurs of that is interpreted, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted «قدم صدق», and مسجد الجامع, صلاة الأولى, حبّ الحصيد and حبّة الحمقاء. Its interpretation is to suppose a qualified noun to which the mentioned muḍāf is annexed; the implied form in these examples is: the foot of a striving of truth (قدم سعي صدق), the mosque of the gathering place (مسجد المكان الجامع), the prayer of the first hour (صلاة الساعة الأولى), and the seed of the foolish herb (حبة البقلة الحمقاء) — they described it as foolish only because it grows in the channels of torrents, so the torrent passes over it and cuts it off and feet tread on it. Among the examples of annexing the adjective to its qualified noun is their saying جَرْدُ قَطِيفة, with fatḥa on the jīm, sukūn on the rāʾ, fatḥa on the qāf and kasra on the ṭāʾ, and سَحْقُ عِمامة, with fatḥa on the sīn, sukūn on the ḥāʾ and kasra on the ʿayn. Its interpretation is likewise to suppose a qualified noun, and to suppose the annexation of the adjective to its genus, with its genus in the genitive by (من), because the annexation is in the sense of (من), i.e. a worn-bare thing from the very velvet, and a worn-out thing of the genus of turban. So "thing" is the qualified noun, and جرد and سحق are its adjective, and the adjective in both is annexed in meaning to its genus.
3- Ibn Hishām and the attachment of «للناس»: Ibn Hishām permitted His saying «للناس» to be attached to (كان), in his discussion concerning attachment to the deficient verb. He said:
"Are they [the preposition phrase and the adverb] attached to the deficient verb? Those who claim that it does not indicate an event (ḥadath) forbade that — namely al-Mubarrad, then al-Fārisī, then Ibn Jinnī, then al-Jurjānī, then Ibn Burhān, then al-Shalawbīn. The correct view is that all of them indicate it except laysa." That is, (كان) indicates an event, namely absolute being, and what restricts it is its khabar. So the meaning of كان زيد is "Zayd came to be", and your saying قائما conveys that what is meant is the occurrence of Zayd's standing. It also indicates a specific time, namely the past; whereas its khabar, قائم, indicates an absolute time, which is restricted and specified by the time in كان or يكون. The result is that (كان) indicates an absolute event restricted by the khabar, and the khabar indicates an absolute time restricted by the time derived from كان; so they compensate each other. As for the rest of the verbs, such as (صار), which indicates transition, and (أصبح), which indicates entering into the morning, etc., their indication of an event not indicated by the khabar is extremely evident. The falsity of the view that they do not indicate an event has been argued by several things, among them: that the base in the verb is the indication of event and time, since what indicates the event alone is a maṣdar and what indicates time alone is a noun of time, and the verb does not leave its base except by evidence. Among them: that verbs equal in time are distinguished only by events; so if that by which they differ were removed and that by which they are equal remained, there would be no difference between كان زيد غنيا and صار زيد غنيا — yet the difference exists, so what entails the opposite is false. And among them: that if their meaning were time, it would be permissible for a complete sentence to be formed from one of them and an abstract noun, just as one is formed from that [abstract noun] and a noun of time. Then Ibn Hishām said:
"Those who affirm that attachment have argued from the saying of Allah the Exalted: «أكان للناس عجبا أن أوحينا», for the lām cannot be attached to (عجبا), because it is a maṣdar placed after [it], nor to (أوحينا), because of the corruption of meaning and because it is the ṣila of (أن). It may also be attached to an omitted ḥāl from (عجبا), in the manner of the poet's saying:
لمية موحشا طلل ... يلوح كأنه خلل
(Mayya has a desolate ruin that gleams as though it were the lining of a sword-sheath.)"
And the wording of Ibn Yaʿīsh: "His saying للناس is attached to (كان). That is because it must be attached either to (عجبا), to (أوحينا), or to (كان). It cannot be attached to (عجبا) itself, because it is a maṣdar and its governed word is part of its ṣila, so it may not precede it; nor can it be an adjective of (عجبا) attached to something omitted, because it precedes it, and the adjective does not precede the qualified noun. Nor can it be attached to (أوحينا), because it is within its ṣila and may not be placed before it. Since its attachment to what we have mentioned is invalid, it is determined that it is attached to (كان) itself, as an adverb is attached to a verb."
I do not know how Ibn Yaʿīsh forbade placing the adjective before the qualified noun, when the grammarians are agreed that if it precedes it, it is parsed as a ḥāl, and they cited the aforementioned verse [as evidence].

dervis-irab:5-6.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الضياء): it may be the plural of ضوء, like سوط and سياط, and حوض and حياض; or it may be the maṣdar (verbal noun) of ضاء يضوء ضياءً وضوءاً, like عاذ يعوذ عياذاً وعوذاً. On either view the muḍāf is omitted, its implied form being: He made the sun possessed of light (ذات ضياء) and the moon possessed of light (ذا نور); and the making [of them] radiance and light [itself] is because of the abundance of that in them. The fine distinction between ضوء and نور was given in Sūrat al-Baqara, so refer back to it.

* I'rab:
(هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ ضِياءً وَالْقَمَرَ نُوراً): (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (الذي) is its khabar (predicate), and the clause (جعل) is the ṣila (relative clause). If جعل is in the sense of "making into", then (الشمس) is a first object and (ضياء) a second object; if جعل is in the sense of "creating", then (الشمس) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and (ضياء) a ḥāl (circumstantial). (القمر نورا) is conjoined to them. (وَقَدَّرَهُ مَنازِلَ لِتَعْلَمُوا عَدَدَ السِّنِينَ وَالْحِسابَ): (قدره) is a verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a direct object. (منازل) means "in stations", so it is accusative as an adverb. The implied form may also be "possessed of stations" (ذا منازل), in which case قدّر is transitive to two objects, because its meaning is "made, rendered", so [منازل] is a second object. It is also possible that قدّر is transitive to one object, in the sense of "created", that object being the hāʾ, with (منازل) as a ḥāl, i.e. moving [through stations]. Abū al-Baqāʾ held a novel view not without merit, namely that the pronoun is accusative by removal of the preposition: the genitive particle was omitted, i.e. "He appointed for it stations", with (منازل) as a direct object. The lām is causal; (تعلموا) is accusative by an implied (أن); (عدد) is a direct object; (السنين) is a muḍāf ilayhi; and (الحساب) is conjoined to (عدد). Abū ʿAmr was asked about (الحساب): "Shall we put it in the accusative or the genitive?" He said: "And who knows the number of the reckoning?" The meaning of his answer is that he was asked whether we conjoin it to (عدد) and so put it in the accusative, or to (السنين) and so put it in the genitive; it is as though he said: it cannot be made genitive, since that would entail that the number of the reckoning is known, and no one is able to know its number. (ما خَلَقَ اللَّهُ ذلِكَ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ يُفَصِّلُ الْآياتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ): (ما) is negative; (خلق الله ذلك) is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a direct object; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (بالحق) is a ḥāl, so the exception is emptied (mufarragh) from the most general of states, i.e. He did not create that except bound up with truth and consummate wisdom, and He did not create it in vain. The clause (يفصل الآيات) is also a ḥāl; (الآيات) is a direct object; (لقوم) is attached to (يفصل); and the clause (يعلمون) is a naʿt (adjective) of (قوم).
(إِنَّ فِي اخْتِلافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ وَما خَلَقَ اللَّهُ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَّقُونَ): the clause is resumptive, to give the reason for the alternation of night and day and their variation by increase and decrease. (إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb; (في اختلاف) is the fronted khabar of (إنّ); (ما) is a relative noun conjoined to (اختلاف); it may also be maṣdar-forming, with the maṣdar conjoined to (اختلاف). (في السموات والأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (خلق). In (لآيات), the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and (آيات) is the postponed noun of (إنّ); (لقوم) is attached to a naʿt of (آيات); and the clause (يتقون) is a naʿt of (قوم).

dervis-irab:7-10.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الرجاء): it has two meanings, both suitable in this verse. The first is fear; from it is the poet's saying:
إذ لسعته النحل لم يرج لسعها ... وخالفها في بيت نوب عواسل
(When the bees stung him he did not fear their sting, and he came at them in their house while they were away — honey-making bees.)
The second is hope; from it is the poet's saying:
أترجو بنو مروان سمعي وطاعتي ... وقومي تميم والفلاة ورائيا
(Do the Banū Marwān hope for my hearing and obedience, when my people are Tamīm and the desert is behind me?)
So the meaning on the first is: they do not fear punishment; and on the second: they do not hope for reward. It is also said that what is meant by الرجاء here is expectation, under which both fear and hope fall.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لا يَرْجُونَ لِقاءَنا): (إنّ) and its noun; the clause (لا يرجون) is the ṣila (relative clause); and (لقاءنا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَرَضُوا بِالْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وَاطْمَأَنُّوا بِها): conjoined to (لا يرجون لقاءنا), so it falls under the ruling of the ṣila. It is possible that the wāw is circumstantial, with (قد) implied; the same is said of (واطمأنوا بها). (وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنْ آياتِنا غافِلُونَ): (الذين) is conjoined to the preceding (الذين), so it is a category distinct from (الذين لا يرجون); a predication is made about both kinds in what follows. (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (عن آياتنا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (غافلون); (غافلون) is the khabar (predicate) of (هم); and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. (أُولئِكَ مَأْواهُمُ النَّارُ بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ): (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; (مأواهم) is a second mubtadaʾ and (النار) is the khabar of the second; the second with its khabar is the khabar of (أولئك); and (أولئك) with its khabar is the khabar of (إنّ). (بما كانوا يكسبون) was covered in the i'rab of (بما كانوا يكفرون).
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ يَهْدِيهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِإِيمانِهِمْ): (إنّ) and its noun; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; (عملوا) is conjoined to (آمنوا) and (الصالحات) is an object; and the clause (يهديهم ربهم) is the khabar of (إنّ). (تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمُ الْأَنْهارُ فِي جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ): the clause is a second khabar of (إنّ), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of (يهديهم), or resumptive. (في جنات النعيم) is a third khabar, or a second ḥāl, or attached to (تجري). (دَعْواهُمْ فِيها سُبْحانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَتَحِيَّتُهُمْ فِيها سَلامٌ): (دعواهم) is a mubtadaʾ; (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (دعواهم) or to an omitted ḥāl; (سبحانك) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and the clause composed of it is the khabar of (دعواهم). The meaning is that their supplication is this very wording, so the khabar is the mubtadaʾ itself. (اللهم) is a vocative, a singular proper noun (munādā mufrad ʿalam), and the doubled mīm is a substitute for the vocative particle. (تحيتهم) is a mubtadaʾ; (فيها) is attached to (تحيتهم) or to an omitted ḥāl; and (سلام) is the khabar of (تحيتهم). The maṣdar (verbal noun), meaning التحية, is annexed to its object, the agent being latent, i.e. Allah's greeting to them, or the angels' greeting of them; or it is annexed to its agent, i.e. they greet one another. (وَآخِرُ دَعْواهُمْ أَنِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (آخر) is a mubtadaʾ and (دعواهم) a muḍāf ilayhi; (أن) is lightened from the heavy (أنّ), its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); (الحمد) is a mubtadaʾ and (لله) the khabar; (رب العالمين) is a naʿt (adjective) of, or a badal (substitute) from, (الله); and the clause (الحمد لله) is the khabar of (أنْ). [Translator's note: the source does not state the khabar of (آخر); it is (أن) with what falls under it.]

dervis-irab:11-12.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ يُعَجِّلُ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ الشَّرَّ اسْتِعْجالَهُمْ بِالْخَيْرِ لَقُضِيَ إِلَيْهِمْ أَجَلُهُمْ): the wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, brought to portray the state of people and give body to what their being contains of compliance with the impulses of the soul, which grows angry and vexed with others, so that in moments of inner crisis supplications escape from them in which they wish death upon their children and their kin. But Allah passes over answering them, because if He answered everything that comes from them, He would have finished with their destruction. (لو) is a conditional particle of impossibility (li-l-imtināʿ); (يعجل) is an imperfect verb and (الله) its fāʿil (agent); (للناس) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يعجل); (الشر) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (استعجالهم) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and (بالخير) is attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun), namely (استعجالهم). The lām falls in the answer of (لو); (قضي) is a passive past verb; (إليهم) is attached to (قضي); and (أجلهم) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The meaning is: their term and their appointed duration would have been finished. More of the splendid subtleties in this graceful expression will come in the section on Rhetoric. This is the well-known parsing; however, Sībawayh parsed (استعجالهم) as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied form in his view being "a hastening like their hastening"; then the qualified noun, namely استعجال, was omitted and its adjective, namely مثل, put in its place, so it remained "and if He hastened like their hastening"; then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place, and it was parsed as a ḥāl from that implied maṣdar. The first is easier, as will come. It may also be parsed as accusative by removal of the preposition, by dropping the kāf of comparison, the implied form being "like their hastening" (كاستعجالهم). (فَنَذَرُ الَّذِينَ لا يَرْجُونَ لِقاءَنا فِي طُغْيانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (نذر) is conjoined to the implied sense of negation, because (لو يعجل) contains the meaning of the negation of hastening, as though it were said: We do not hasten evil for them nor finish their term for them, so We leave… Its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "We". (الذين) is a direct object; the clause (لا يرجون لقاءنا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (في طغيانهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يعمهون); and the clause (يعمهون) is a ḥāl, i.e. wavering in their blindness, stumbling in the darknesses of their sins. (وَإِذا مَسَّ الْإِنْسانَ الضُّرُّ): the wāw is for resumption and the clause is resumptive, brought to establish man's weakness and the extremity of his helplessness. (إذا) is an adverb for future time, and the clause (مس) is in a genitive construct with it; (الإنسان) is a direct object and (الضر) is the agent. (دَعانا لِجَنْبِهِ أَوْ قاعِداً أَوْ قائِماً): the clause (دعانا) has no grammatical position because it is the answer of (إذا). (لجنبه) is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of (دعانا), as shown by the two ḥāls that are conjoined to it; (أو) is a conjunction and (قاعدا) is conjoined to the position of (لجنبه), and likewise (أو قائما). The meaning of these states is that the afflicted person keeps on constantly voicing supplication, not slackening from it in any state whatsoever, whether he is lying prostrate, unable to rise, or sitting feebly, unable to stand, or standing, unable to walk. (فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنا عَنْهُ ضُرَّهُ مَرَّ كَأَنْ لَمْ يَدْعُنا إِلى ضُرٍّ مَسَّهُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (لما) is temporal (ḥīniyya) or linking (rābiṭa); (كشفنا) is a verb and its agent; (عنه) is attached to (كشفنا); the clause (مر) has no grammatical position because it is the answer of (لما). (كأن) is lightened from the heavy (كأنّ), its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause (لم يدعنا) is its khabar (predicate); (إلى ضر) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يدعنا); and the clause (مسه) is a naʿt (adjective) of (ضر). (كَذلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): (كذلك) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. like that adorning; (زين) is passive; (للمسرفين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (زين); (ما) is a relative noun, the deputy agent; the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila; the wāw is the noun of (كان), and the clause (يعملون) is the khabar of (كان).

* Rhetoric:
1- Tankīt (a deliberate choice for a subtle point) in the saying of Allah the Exalted «ولو يعجل الله للناس الشر استعجالهم بالخير». The flow of the speech required bringing the maṣdar matching its verb, namely التعجيل, but He turned instead to الاستعجال, which is the maṣdar of استعجل [Translator's note: the source prints «لاستعجال»], for a point that is subtle for the understanding and from which minds are almost distracted. For placing a maṣdar as an emphasis alongside a verb other than its own in the Mighty Book is hardly ever without a subtle point. The most the grammarians say about this is that the maṣdar was made to run on the verb with the extra letters [of the derived form] supposed absent. But when the perceptive reader climbs with his thought the steps of eloquence, he knows that behind the inclination to this maṣdar in place of the maṣdar suited to the verb lies a secret: الاستعجال was put in place of التعجيل to announce and signal the speed of His answering them and fulfilling their requests, so that it is as though their seeking haste for good were [His] hastening for them. Similar to that is His saying «والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا», in drawing attention to the inevitability of [divine] power taking effect in what is decreed and the swiftness of carrying out the ruling; it will come in its place.
2- Taqsīm (division), or ṣiḥḥat al-aqsām (soundness of the divisions): it consists in the speaker's exhausting all the divisions of the meaning he is engaged in, so that he leaves none of it out. His saying «دعانا لجنبه أو قاعدا أو قائما» exhausted all the postures in which a person may be. Taqsīm has recurred in Āl ʿImrān, so refer back to it.

dervis-irab:13-17.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْقُرُونَ): plural of قَرْن, with fatḥa on the qāf, which is the people of each age; they were so named because of their being joined (muqārana) to one another. From it comes the ram's horn (قرن الكبش), because of its being paired with another opposite it. القِرن, with kasra on the qāf, is one who stands up to his peer (qarīn) in combat. It is also gathered from the lexicons that القَرن, with fatḥa on the qāf, is a hundred years; a nation after a nation; and time in general; and القرون الخالية are the nations that preceded those after them.
(خَلائِفَ): plural of خليفة, which is one who succeeds another and stands in his place, and the imam above whom there is no imam. It is masculine, so one says هذا خليفة آخر; sometimes it is treated as feminine with regard to its form, so one says خليفة أخرى. It is pluralised as خلفاء and خلائف. The numeral with the first plural is masculine, so one says ثلاثة خلفاء; with the second it may be masculine or feminine, so one says ثلاثة خلائف and ثلاث خلائف.
(القرآن): there are five views about the word Qur'an, which we summarise as follows:
1- What al-Shāfiʿī held: that it is neither hamzated nor derived, but was coined as a proper name for the revealed speech.
2- What is reported from al-Ashʿarī and others: that it is derived from قرنت الشيء بالشيء ("I joined the thing to the thing"), when you attach it to it; then it was made a proper name for the revealed wording. It was so named because the sūras, verses and letters in it are joined to one another.
3- Al-Farrāʾ held that it is derived from القرائن (corroborating indications), because the verses in it confirm one another, and it was made a proper name for the revealed wording for that reason. On these two [latter] views it is likewise not hamzated, like the one before them, and its nūn is radical.
4- Al-Zajjāj said: it is a descriptive on the pattern faʿlān, hamzated, derived from القَرْء in the sense of gathering; from it is قرأت الماء في الحوض, when you gathered it. The speech revealed to the Prophet who was sent with it was named Qur'an because it gathered the sūras, or gathered the fruits of the previous books.
5- What al-Liḥyānī and a group held: that it is a hamzated maṣdar (verbal noun) on the pattern of الغفران, by which what is read was named — naming the object by the maṣdar.
Al-Suyūṭī reports in al-Itqān from al-Jāḥiẓ that Allah named His Book with a name different from what the Arabs named their speech: He named the whole a Qur'an, as the Arabs named the whole of their speech a dīwān; He named part of it a sūra, like a qaṣīda; He named part of a sūra an āya, like a verse-line (bayt); and He named the end of a sūra [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably the end of a verse] a fāṣila, like the rhyme (qāfiya).
As for the Encyclopaedia of Islam, it begins its discussion in the article "Qur'an" by mentioning the Muslims' disagreement over the pronunciation, derivation and meaning of the word Qur'an. Some of them say al-Qurān without hamza and hold that it is a word coined as the words Tawrāt and Injīl were coined — which, as you see, is the view of al-Shāfiʿī. Then the Encyclopaedia goes on to mention the rest of the five views mentioned above and adds a sixth view to them, namely what Schwally and Wellhausen held: that the word is Hebrew or Syriac and that its meaning is "what is read". The Encyclopaedia inclines, with these two scholars, to their view, which holds that qaraʾa in the sense of "recite" is not a word of Arabic lineage but is a loanword in the language.
More of this interesting discussion will come in other places in which the most preferable of the views will become clear.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنَا الْقُرُونَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ): the wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of verification; (أهلكنا القرون) is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and an object; (من قبلكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أهلكنا). It cannot be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (القرون), because it is an adverb of time, and so it does not occur as a ḥāl from a concrete entity, just as it does not occur as a khabar (predicate) for it; this has been discussed before. (لَمَّا ظَلَمُوا وَجاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ): (لما) is temporal (ḥīniyya), attached to (أهلكنا), or linking (rābiṭa); (ظلموا) is a verb and its agent. In (وجاءتهم), the wāw is the wāw of circumstance (wāw al-ḥāl), with (قد) implied — the discussion of the wāw of circumstance has been given before; it is also said that the wāw is for conjunction with (ظلموا), but perhaps the first is preferable. (جاءتهم رسلهم) is a verb, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and an agent; (بالبينات) is attached to (جاءتهم). (وَما كانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْقَوْمَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ): conjoined to (ظلموا). The lām in (ليؤمنوا) is of denial (lām al-juḥūd), and (يؤمنوا) is accusative by an implied (أن); it with what it enters on is the khabar of (كانوا). (كذلك) is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar; (نجزي القوم) is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a direct object; and (المجرمين) is a naʿt of (القوم). (ثُمَّ جَعَلْناكُمْ خَلائِفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ): (ثم) is a conjunction; (جعلناكم) is conjoined to (أهلكنا); (خلائف) is a second direct object; (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt of (خلائف); and (من بعدهم) is attached to (جعلناكم). (لِنَنْظُرَ كَيْفَ تَعْمَلُونَ): the lām is causal and (ننظر) is accusative by an implied (أن) after it. (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as the object of (تعملون), i.e. so that We may see what deed you do — not [the object] of (ننظر), because it has the right to stand first, so what precedes it cannot govern it. It is not far-fetched that it be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. in what state you do the deeds befitting succession.
(وَإِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُنا بَيِّناتٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, and the clause (تتلى) is in a genitive construct with it; (تتلى) is a passive imperfect verb; (عليهم) is attached to (تتلى); (آياتنا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and (بينات) is a ḥāl.
(قالَ الَّذِينَ لا يَرْجُونَ لِقاءَنَا: ائْتِ بِقُرْآنٍ غَيْرِ هذا أَوْ بَدِّلْهُ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer of (إذا). (الذين) is the agent; the clause (لا يرجون) is the ṣila (relative clause); (لقاءنا) is the object of (يرجون); the clause (ائت) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); (بقرآن) is attached to (ائت); (غير) is a naʿt of (قرآن) and (هذا) is in a genitive construct with (غير); (أو) is a conjunction and (بدله) is conjoined to (ائت).
(قُلْ: ما يَكُونُ لِي أَنْ أُبَدِّلَهُ مِنْ تِلْقاءِ نَفْسِي): (ما) is negative; (يكون) is a deficient imperfect verb; (لي) is its fronted khabar; and (أن) with what falls under it is its postponed noun. It may also be complete (tāmma), with the maṣdar as agent. (من تلقاء نفسي) is attached to (أبدله), and (نفسي) is in a genitive construct with (تلقاء); the discussion of التلقاء has been given before. (إِنْ أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا ما يُوحى إِلَيَّ): (إن) is negative; (أتبع) is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "I"; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (ما) is a direct object; and the clause (يوحى إلي) is the ṣila. (إِنِّي أَخافُ إِنْ عَصَيْتُ رَبِّي عَذابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ): (إنّ) and its noun, and the clause (أخاف) is its khabar; (إن) is conditional; (عصيت) is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is the agent; (ربي) is a direct object; (عذاب) is a direct object of (أخاف); (يوم) is a muḍāf ilayhi; and (عظيم) is a naʿt. (قُلْ لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما تَلَوْتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلا أَدْراكُمْ بِهِ): (لو) is conditional; (شاء الله) is a verb and its agent; the clause (ما تلوته عليكم) is the answer of (لو); (عليكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تلوته). In (ولا), the wāw is a conjunction and (لا) is negative; (أدراكم) is a past verb whose agent is latent, the kāf being a direct object; and (به) is attached to (أدراكم). (فَقَدْ لَبِثْتُ فِيكُمْ عُمُراً مِنْ قَبْلِهِ أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ): the fāʾ is causal (taʿlīliyya); (قد) is a particle of verification; (لبثت) is a verb and its agent; (فيكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; (عمرا) is an adverb of time attached to (لبثت); and (من قبله) is attached to (لبثت). In (أفلا), the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (istifhām inkārī), the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to something implied, (لا) is negative, and (تعقلون) is conjoined to the implied [verb]. (فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِآياتِهِ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (من) is an interrogative noun in the sense of negation, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (أظلم) is its khabar; (ممن) is attached to (أظلم); the clause (افترى) is the ṣila of the relative noun; (على الله) is attached to (افترى); and (كذبا) is a direct object. (أو) is a conjunction; (كذب) is conjoined to (افترى); and (بآياته) is attached to (كذب). The meaning is: no one is more unjust than one who fabricated lies against Allah. The addition of (كذبا), even though fabrication is never anything but a lie, is to show that this, besides being a fabrication against Allah, is a lie in itself; for a fabrication may be a lie only in the attribution, as when one attributes Zayd's sin to ʿAmr.
(إِنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ): the clause gives the reason for there being none more unjust than one who fabricated a lie against Allah or denied His signs. (إنّ) and its noun, and the clause (لا يفلح) is its khabar; (المجرمون) is the agent.

dervis-irab:18-20.t:
* I'rab:
(وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلا يَنْفَعُهُمْ): the wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, to relate another of their crimes. (يعبدون) is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (من دون الله) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of (يعبدون), i.e. going beyond Allah — not in the sense of abandoning Allah entirely, but in the sense of not being content with it [i.e. with His worship] and adding the worship of idols to it for intercession and drawing near. (ما) is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); it refers to the idols, but He observed its form and so used the singular in His saying (ما لا يضرهم ولا ينفعهم), and observed its meaning in His saying (هؤلاء شفعاؤنا) and so used the plural. The clause (لا يضرهم) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and (ولا ينفعهم) is conjoined. It is also said that (ما) is a qualified indefinite (mawṣūfa). (وَيَقُولُونَ هؤُلاءِ شُفَعاؤُنا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (يقولون) is conjoined to (يعبدون); (هؤلاء) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (شفعاؤنا) the khabar (predicate); and (عند الله) is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl. (قُلْ أَتُنَبِّئُونَ اللَّهَ بِما لا يَعْلَمُ فِي السَّماواتِ وَلا فِي الْأَرْضِ): (قل) is an imperative verb, and the clause (أتنبئون) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); what is intended by the command is to silence them with reproof. The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (istifhām inkārī), as though He were rebuking them and disapproving of their informing Him of what He does not know to have any existence in the heavens and the earth, namely the intercessor; had there been an intercessor there, He would have known him. «وربما» [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently a misprint for «وبما», "and in (بما)"]: the bāʾ is a genitive particle, and (ما) is a relative noun or a qualified indefinite; on both suppositions the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. [what] He knows it [not]. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (تنبئون); (في السموات) is a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun in (يعلم); and the clause (لا يعلم) is the ṣila of (ما). (سُبْحانَهُ وَتَعالى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ): it has been stated before that (سبحانه) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; (تعالى) is a past verb; (عما يشركون) is attached to (تعالى); and (ما) is relative or maṣdar-forming.
(وَما كانَ النَّاسُ إِلَّا أُمَّةً واحِدَةً فَاخْتَلَفُوا): the wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, brought to show that innate nature (fiṭra) and divine legislation call for the unity of mankind, but they differed out of their inclination towards the whims of the soul and its demands. The commentators have expounded at length on how that came about; it may be consulted in the extensive works. (ما) is negative; (كان الناس) is (كان) and its noun; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (أمة) is the khabar of (كان) and (واحدة) a naʿt (adjective). (فاختلفوا) is conjoined according to the sense, i.e. all people were upon the truth, then they differed. (وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ فِيما فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لولا) is a particle of impossibility because of existence (ḥarf imtināʿ li-wujūd); (كلمة) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; the clause (سبقت) is a naʿt of (كلمة); and (من ربك) is attached to (سبقت). In (لقضي), the lām is [in] the answer of (لولا), and the clause (قضي) has no grammatical position because it is the answer of a non-jussive condition. The nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "the matter"; (بينهم) is attached to (قضي), i.e. He would have decided between them and distinguished the one in the right from the one in the wrong; but His word had gone before with postponement, so that this abode be the abode of obligation and that one the abode of reward or punishment. (فيما) is also attached to (قضي); (فيه) is attached to (يختلفون); and the clause (يختلفون) is the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَيَقُولُونَ لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (يقولون) is an imperfect verb and its agent; (لولا) is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); (أنزل) is a passive past verb; (عليه) is attached to (أنزل); (آية) is the deputy agent; and (من ربه) is a naʿt of (آية). The imperfect was used to make present the image of what they said.
(فَقُلْ إِنَّمَا الْغَيْبُ لِلَّهِ فَانْتَظِرُوا إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الْمُنْتَظِرِينَ): the fāʾ falls in the answer of (لولا) [Translator's note: so in the source; (لولا) here is of urging, and the fāʾ is commonly taken as linking the reply to their request]; (إنما) is a restrictive particle, "the restraining and the restrained" (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (الغيب) is a mubtadaʾ and (لله) the khabar. In (فانتظروا), the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa and (انتظروا) is an imperative verb and its agent. (إني): (إنّ) and its noun; (من المنتظرين) is its khabar; and (معكم) is an adverb attached to (المنتظرين).

dervis-irab:21-23.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْفُلْكِ): ships. They were called فلك because of their going round (dawarān) in the water; its root sense is turning round. From it comes فلكة المغزل (the whorl of the spindle), and تفلّك ثدي الجارية, when the girl's breast became round. الفلك may be plural or singular; here it is plural.
(رِيحٌ): in al-Miṣbāḥ: "The wind (الريح) is the air made subservient between heaven and earth. Its original [middle letter] is wāw, but it was changed [into yāʾ] because of the kasra before it. The plural is أرواح and رياح; some say أرياح, with yāʾ, after the form of the singular, and Abū Ḥātim judged that a mistake. الريح is feminine for the most part, so one says هي الريح; it may be masculine in the sense of 'the air', so one says هو الريح — Abū Zayd reported this. Ibn al-Anbārī said: الريح is feminine without a [feminine] marker, and likewise all its names except الإعصار, which is masculine. راح اليوم يروح روحاً, of the pattern of قال — and in one dialect of the pattern of خاف — when its wind became strong; so it is رائح."
(عاصِفٌ): عصفت الريح, so it is عاصف and عاصفة. The poet said:
حتى إذا عصفت ريح مزعزعة ... فيها قطار ورعد صوته زجل
(Until, when a shaking wind blew violently, bearing rain and thunder whose sound was a roar…)
One also says أعصفت الريح, so it is معصفة and معصف; the plural is معاصف and معاصيف.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذا أَذَقْنَا النَّاسَ رَحْمَةً مِنْ بَعْدِ ضَرَّاءَ مَسَّتْهُمْ إِذا لَهُمْ مَكْرٌ فِي آياتِنا):
the wāw is resumptive; (إذا) is an adverb for future time, putting its condition in the genitive and accusative by its answer; the clause (أذقنا) is in the position of genitive by annexation to it. Its answer is in the second (إذا), the (إذا) of surprise (fujāʾiyya); it was made the answer only because it has the sense of surprise, as though He said: and when We have mercy on them after hardship, they surprise [us] with the occurrence of what is hateful from them and hasten to it. The discussion of the (إذا) of surprise, and whether it is a particle, an adverb of time or an adverb of place, has been given before. (رحمة) is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من بعد) is a naʿt (adjective) of (رحمة); (ضراء) is «مضافة ترجمة» [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently a misprint for مضاف إليه, "a muḍāf ilayhi"]; the clause (مستهم) is a naʿt of (ضراء). (إذا) is of surprise; (لهم) is a fronted khabar (predicate) and (مكر) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and (في آياتنا) is a naʿt of (مكر). (قُلِ اللَّهُ أَسْرَعُ مَكْراً): (الله) is a mubtadaʾ, (أسرع) is the khabar, and (مكرا) is a tamyīz (specification). (إِنَّ رُسُلَنا يَكْتُبُونَ ما تَمْكُرُونَ): (إنّ) and its noun, and the clause (يكتبون) is its khabar; (ما) is a relative noun, a direct object, and the clause (تمكرون) is the ṣila (relative clause). The clause gives the reason for the swiftness of His the Exalted's plotting and His hastening the punishment. (هُوَ الَّذِي يُسَيِّرُكُمْ فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ): a resumptive clause, brought to set out another of their crimes, based on the variation in the fluctuation that comes over them in relation to the ease and hardship that befall them. (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (الذي) its khabar; the clause (يسيركم) is the ṣila, the kāf being a direct object; and (في البر والبحر) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يسيركم). (حَتَّى إِذا كُنْتُمْ فِي الْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِمْ بِرِيحٍ طَيِّبَةٍ وَفَرِحُوا بِها): (حتى) is a particle of limit and genitive; (إذا) is an adverb for future time, and the clause (كنتم) is in a genitive construct with it; the tāʾ is the noun of (كان) and (في الفلك) is its khabar. (جرين) is conjoined to (كنتم) by way of shift of person (iltifāt), as will come in the section on Rhetoric; the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil (agent) of (جرين); (بهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (جرين); (بريح طيبة) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. being driven, and (طيبة) is a naʿt. (وفرحوا بها) is conjoined to (وجرين); it may also be a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in (بهم), with (قد) implied.
(جاءَتْها رِيحٌ عاصِفٌ وَجاءَهُمُ الْمَوْجُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكانٍ): the clause (جاءتها) has no grammatical position because it is the answer of (إذا); (ريح) is the agent of (جاءتها) and (عاصف) a naʿt; (جاءهم الموج) is conjoined to (جاءتها); (من كل مكان) is attached to (جاءهم), or to an omitted ḥāl from (الموج), i.e. descending. (وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ أُحِيطَ بِهِمْ): conjoined to (جاءهم); (أنّ) with what falls under it stands in place of the two objects of (ظنوا); and the clause (أحيط بهم) is the khabar of (أنهم). The reader will notice that He made the condition three things — being in the ships, their sailing with them by a good wind, and rejoicing in it — and made the answer three things as well — the coming of the stormy wind, the coming of the waves, and their thinking they were encompassed.
(دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ): the clause (دعوا الله) is a badal (substitute) from (ظنوا), a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), because of the connection and mutual entailment between them; that is because their supplication is a necessary consequence of their thinking they would perish, so it is bound up with it. Or it is resumptive, built on a question that comes to mind, namely: so what did they do? and it was said: they called on Allah. (دعوا الله) is a verb, its agent and an object; (مخلصين) is a ḥāl; (له) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (مخلصين); and (الدين) is a direct object. (لَئِنْ أَنْجَيْتَنا مِنْ هذِهِ لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ): the lām paves the way for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); (إن) is conditional; «نجيتنا» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has (أنجيتنا)] is a verb, its agent and a direct object, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (من هذه) is attached to (أنجيتنا), the reference being to the terrors and the brink of destruction they fell into at sea. (لنكونن) is its [the oath's] answer, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because the oath came first. The oath and its answer are in the position of accusative by an implied saying, and that implied saying is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; the implied form is: they called on Allah, saying: if You save us from these terrors, we shall surely be among the thankful. (فَلَمَّا أَنْجاهُمْ إِذا هُمْ يَبْغُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (لما) is temporal (ḥīniyya) or linking (rābiṭa); (أنجاهم) is a verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a direct object; (إذا) is of surprise; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يبغون) is its khabar; (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يبغون); and (بغير الحق) is a ḥāl. (يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّما بَغْيُكُمْ عَلى أَنْفُسِكُمْ): (إنما) is "the restraining and the restrained" (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (بغيكم) is a mubtadaʾ and (على أنفسكم) the khabar. (مَتاعَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): Ḥafṣ, Ibn Isḥāq and al-Mufaḍḍal read (متاعَ) in the accusative, as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. you enjoy the enjoyment of the life of this world; or as a direct object of an omitted verb, i.e. you seek the enjoyment of the life of this world. The rest read it in the nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. it is the enjoyment of the life of this world. Other things have also been said, but what we have mentioned is the most likely. (ثُمَّ إِلَيْنا مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَنُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ): (ثم) is a conjunction of delay; (إلينا) is a fronted khabar and (مرجعكم) a postponed mubtadaʾ. In (فننبئكم), the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (ننبئكم) is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object. «وربما كنتم تعملون» [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently a misprint for «وبما»]: [بما] is attached to (ننبئكم); the clause (كنتم) is the ṣila of (ما); and the clause (تعملون) is the khabar of (كنتم).

* Rhetoric:
In these verses there are several kinds of rhetoric, some of which have been mentioned before, while others need further elaboration. Among the most important of its arts are:
1- The shift of person (iltifāt) from address to the third person, then the return to the third person [Translator's note: so in the source], in the saying of Allah the Exalted «هو الذي يسيركم في البر والبحر» to the end of the verse. The discussion of iltifāt has been given before, and we clarify it here, saying: since His saying (هو الذي يسيركم) is an address that contains the bestowing of favour and the display of the blessing upon those addressed, and since those made to travel by land and sea are believers and unbelievers, and the address includes them all, it was fitting to address them with it, so that the righteous may continue in thankfulness and the wicked may perhaps remember this blessing, so that his heart is readied to remember and thank the One who bestowed it. And since at the end of the verse there is what entails that, when saved, they act wrongfully in the land, He turned from addressing them with that to the third person, so as not to address the believers with what is not fitting to issue from them, namely wrongdoing without right. That is from one angle. From another angle, He mentioned their state to others in order to make them marvel at it, as one informing them, and to call forth from them disapproval of them and denunciation of what they committed. So in the iltifāt there are two benefits, namely exaggeration and loathing and distancing. Al-Rāzī said: "The transition from the station of address to the station of absence in this place is a sign of loathing and distancing, just as the reverse of that in His saying إياك نعبد is a sign of good pleasure and drawing near."
2- The loose metonymic trope (al-majāz al-mursal): in His saying «بغيكم على أنفسكم», because wrongdoing does not fall upon the selves; it is rather the evil consequence [that falls upon them], and since wrongdoing is its cause, He mentioned it by way of majāz mursal, the relation being causality.
3- Mushākala (verbal assimilation): the word الريح was made singular for mushākala for two reasons: because it stands opposite His saying, glory be to Him: «جاءتهم ريح عاصف» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads (جاءتها ريح عاصف)]; and because mercy here requires the oneness of the wind, for the ship sails only by one wind, and if the winds differed against it, it would perish; that is why it was emphasised by the description "good".
And in naming the punishment of Allah, glory be to Him, "plotting" (makr) there is the art of mushākala; it has been discussed before.
4- Ishāra (allusion): in His saying (قل الله أسرع مكرا) there is the art of allusion, because the elative indicates that their plotting was swift, but the plotting of Allah is swifter than it. The (إذا) of surprise conveys swiftness, and the meaning is that they came out suddenly with plotting, i.e. they carried it out in the manner of suddenness and speed.

* Benefits:
In the saying of Allah the Exalted: «هو الذي يسيركم في البر والبحر حتى إذا كنتم…» there is a benefit without equal, on which juristic rulings are based, which we point out. It is what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned in his Kashshāf; he said: "If you say: how did He make being in the ships the limit of the travelling by sea, when travelling by sea comes only after being in the ships? I say: He did not make being in the ships the limit of the travelling, but rather the content of the conditional sentence occurring after (حتى), with what falls under it, as though it were said: He makes you travel until, when this event happened, and such and such took place — the coming of the stormy wind, the piling up of the waves, the thought of destruction and the supplication for rescue…" to the end of this passage. Something like this verse came earlier, and we missed pointing out this secret in its place, namely the saying of Allah the Exalted in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ «وابتلوا اليتامى حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح فإن آنستم منهم رشدا فادفعوا إليهم أموالهم». Al-Zamakhsharī used it as evidence for Abū Ḥanīfa's view that the minor is tested before puberty, by handing over to him an amount of wealth with which he is tested — contrary to Mālik, who does not hold that testing takes place before puberty. As for al-Shāfiʿī, he has two views, one agreeing with Abū Ḥanīfa and the other agreeing with Mālik. The imams have discussions on this matter that go beyond the scope of the book; we have only pointed out the place of the rhetorical and grammatical benefit, and for knowledge of the juristic rulings one should refer to the relevant sources.

dervis-irab:57-61.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ قَدْ جاءَتْكُمْ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); جاءتكم موعظة is a verb, a direct object and an agent; and من ربكم is an adjective of موعظة, in which case من is partitive; or it is attached to جاءتكم, in which case it denotes the starting point. (وَشِفاءٌ لِما فِي الصُّدُورِ وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ)
وشفاء is conjoined to موعظة. شفاء is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) that has been made an adjective for emphasis, or it is a noun for that by which one is healed and treated. ولما في الصدور may be an adjective of شفاء, and so be attached to an omitted word; or the lām may be redundant (zāʾida) before the direct object, with في الصدور as the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. هدى and رحمة are likewise conjoined, and للمؤمنين is an adjective. (قُلْ بِفَضْلِ اللَّهِ وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ فَبِذلِكَ فَلْيَفْرَحُوا هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ) The bāʾ is attached to an omitted word. The original wording was: ليفرحوا بفضل الله وبرحمته فبذلك. Then the preposition and its genitive noun were put before the verb to give the sense of restriction; then the fāʾ was inserted to give the sense of causation, so that it became بفضل الله وبرحمته فليفرحوا. Then He said فبذلك فليفرحوا for emphasis and confirmation. Then the first verb was omitted because the second indicates it. The first fāʾ is the fāʾ of the apodosis (jazāʾiyya) and the second is for causation. Then they said: the fāʾ that enters upon بذلك is redundant, and بذلك is a substitute (badal) for بفضل. But it is preferable that it be a conjunction, with بذلك conjoined to بفضل الله; that is sounder than making it redundant. As for the fāʾ that enters upon فليفرحوا, it is the eloquent (faṣīḥa) fāʾ, because it enters with the sense of a condition, as if it were said: "if they rejoice in anything, let them single these two out for rejoicing, for there is nothing more deserving of joy and more refreshing to the breasts than the two of them." هو is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and خير the khabar (predicate); مما is attached to خير, and يجمعون is the ṣila of ما. (قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ مِنْ رِزْقٍ) أرأيتم: it has already been said that it means "tell me". وما أنزل الله: ما is a relative noun, an object of أرأيتم or of أنزل; the clause أنزل is the ṣila and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. أنزله الله.
