It is also possible that ما is interrogative, in the position of the accusative governed by أنزل, and it is then suspended (muʿallaqa) from governing أرأيتم. It is also possible that it is interrogative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, with the clause آلله أذن لكم as the khabar. ولكم is attached to أنزل, and من رزق is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(فَجَعَلْتُمْ مِنْهُ حَراماً وَحَلالًا قُلْ آللَّهُ أَذِنَ لَكُمْ أَمْ عَلَى اللَّهِ تَفْتَرُونَ) فجعلتم is conjoined to أنزل; جعلتم is a verb and an agent; منه is attached to جعلتم; حراما is the object of جعلتم and حلالا is conjoined to it. آلله: the hamza is for denunciatory interrogation (istifhām inkārī), الله is the mubtadaʾ and the clause أذن is its khabar; لكم is attached to أذن. أم is either discontinuous (munqaṭiʿa), meaning بل, or continuous (muttaṣila), i.e. "Did Allah permit you, or do you lie against Him?" Its being continuous is probably the more evident. على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يفترون. (وَما ظَنُّ الَّذِينَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is interrogative, a mubtadaʾ, and ظن is its khabar; الذين is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive complement); the clause يفترون is a ṣila; على الله is attached to يفترون; الكذب is a direct object; and يوم القيامة is an adverbial attached to الظن. The meaning is: what do the fabricators think that He will do to them on that Day? The two objects of ظن are replaced by the implied أن and what follows it. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَشْكُرُونَ) إن and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ذو فضل is its khabar; على الناس is attached to فضل. ولكن: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or resumptive; ولكن and its noun, and the clause لا يشكرون is its khabar. (وَما تَكُونُ فِي شَأْنٍ وَما تَتْلُوا مِنْهُ مِنْ قُرْآنٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; تكون is an imperfect defective verb (nāqiṣ) whose noun is a latent pronoun, i.e. "you"; في شأن is the khabar of تكون. And ما: the wāw is a conjunction and ما is negative; تتلو is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; منه is attached to تتلو. The pronoun refers either to القرآن or to الشأن; in the latter case من is causal, i.e. "because of the matter in which you were engaged"; and من is redundant, and قرآن is a direct object in position, i.e. "and you do not recite of the revelation any Qur'an", because every part of it is Qur'an. The use of a pronoun before the noun is mentioned (iḍmār qabl al-dhikr) is for magnification.
(وَلا تَعْمَلُونَ مِنْ عَمَلٍ إِلَّا كُنَّا عَلَيْكُمْ شُهُوداً إِذْ تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ) ولا تعملون is conjoined to what precedes; من is a redundant preposition and عمل is a direct object in position, or an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq); إلا is a particle of restriction; كنا: kāna and its noun; عليكم is attached to شهودا, i.e. "witnesses"; and شهودا is the khabar of كنا. شهود is the plural of شاهد, and so is إشهاد. إذ is an adverbial for the past, attached to شهودا; the clause تفيضون is added (muḍāf) to the adverbial; and فيه is attached to تفيضون. (وَما يَعْزُبُ عَنْ رَبِّكَ مِنْ مِثْقالِ ذَرَّةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا فِي السَّماءِ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; عن ربك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يعزب; من is a redundant preposition and مثقال ذرة is the agent of يعزب in position; في الأرض is a ḥāl of مثقال ذرة, or an adjective; ولا في السماء is conjoined. (وَلا أَصْغَرَ مِنْ ذلِكَ وَلا أَكْبَرَ إِلَّا فِي كِتابٍ مُبِينٍ) The wāw is resumptive and the sentence is resumptive, brought to confirm what precedes; لا is the lā of generic negation and أصغر is its noun; من ذلك is attached to أصغر; ولا أكبر is conjoined to ولا أصغر; إلا is a particle of restriction; في كتاب مبين is the khabar of لا, and مبين is an adjective of كتاب.
The wording of Ibn Hishām in al-Mughnī: "As for the saying of the Exalted: ﴿وما يعزب عن ربك من مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء ولا أصغر من ذلك ولا أكبر﴾, the apparent position is that it is permissible for أصغر and أكبر to be conjoined to the word مثقال or to its position; and he allowed that لا with the fatḥa is the lā of exoneration (tabriʾa) and with the nominative is either inoperative or operating like ليس. What strengthens the conjunction is that in Sūrat Sabaʾ, in His saying, Glorified and Exalted is He: ﴿عالم الغيب لا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة﴾ [the verse], it is read only with the nominative, since the genitive is not found in the word مثقال. But it is problematic that absence is established together with the establishment of the Book, just as if you said "I did not pass by a man except in the house" it would be a report that your passing by a man in the house was established. When this is ruled out, it is determined that the pause is at السماء and that what follows is resumptive. And when that is established in Sūrat Yūnus we say it in Sūrat Sabaʾ too, that the pause is at الأرض and that the fatḥa did not come in it only out of following the transmission. Some allowed the conjunction in both, on the basis that the meaning of يعزب is not 'to be hidden' but 'to come out into existence'."

* Rhetoric:
In His saying: «وما يعزب عن ربك من مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء» the earth is mentioned before the heaven, though it rightly should come later, because the earth is a part of the heaven and of the orbs and swimming stars in it, and is a very tiny part, which rightly should be put later. But He inclined to put it first because He is in the course of speaking of the earth and mentioning His witnessing of the affairs of the people of the earth, their conditions, their deeds and their livelihoods, and He joined that to His saying «وما يعزب», harmonizing the two so that the meaning follows the meaning. If it is said: the earth has been put before the heaven in many places of the Qur'an, we say: when it comes first in mention, there must be a reason that required it, even if that reason is hidden; some researchers deduce it and others do not. There will come, in its places in this book, some of the marvels of fronting and delaying that will astonish minds.

* Benefits:
In His saying «إلا في كتاب مبين» there is an evident difficulty: what is the reality of this exception, and is it connected (muttaṣil) or discontinuous (munqaṭiʿ)? Making it connected is problematic, because the meaning would become "except in a Book, so it is absent", which is invalid. It is therefore preferable to make it discontinuous, with إلا meaning لكن, and the meaning: nothing is absent from your Lord, but all things are in a Book. Al-Fakhr al-Rāzī tried to make it connected with a long statement, the gist of which is that he made it an exception of the complete type from the most general of circumstances (istithnāʾ mufarragh min aʿamm al-aḥwāl), saying that it is a ḥāl of أصغر and أكبر, and that it is equivalent in force to a connected exception, and that one may say of it neither connected nor discontinuous.

dervis-irab:24-25.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الزخرف): with ḍamma on the zāy, gold, and the perfection of a thing's beauty; of speech, its beauty; of the earth, the colours of its plants.
(ازَّيَّنَتْ): its origin is تزينت; the tāʾ was assimilated into the zāy and the zāy was given a sukūn, so a hamzat al-waṣl (connecting hamza) was brought in for it.
(تَغْنَ): the imperfect of غني بالمكان, "he stayed in the place"; المغاني are dwellings. al-Nābigha said:
غنيت بذلك إذ هم لك جيرة ... منها بعطف رسالة وتودّد
(I dwelt there, when they were your neighbours, in her company, with the inclination of a message and of affection.)
In al-Qāmūs there is what implies that غني also comes in the sense of "to be" and "to be found", as in the saying:
غنيت دارنا بتهامة
that is, "our house was in Tihāma."

* I'rab:
(إِنَّما مَثَلُ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا كَماءٍ أَنْزَلْناهُ مِنَ السَّماءِ): a resumptive speech, conveyed to explain the condition of this world and the swiftness of its passing, and that after it has captivated the eyes with its splendour it leads its people to shed one another's blood and draw the sword among themselves, clouding the purity of the peace that ought to prevail among them; and a likeness is struck for this in the form of a composite simile. إنما: kāffa and makfūfa (a restraining particle and the restrained); مثل is a mubtadaʾ (subject); الحياة is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) and الدنيا an adjective. كماء: the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar (predicate) of مثل, or else كـ is a noun, in which case it is itself the khabar. The clause أنزلناه is an adjective of ماء, and من السماء is attached to أنزلناه.
(فَاخْتَلَطَ بِهِ نَباتُ الْأَرْضِ مِمَّا يَأْكُلُ النَّاسُ وَالْأَنْعامُ): The فاء is a conjunction; اختلط is conjoined to أنزلناه; به is attached to اختلط; نبات الأرض is the fāʿil (agent) of اختلط; مما يأكل الناس, the preposition and its genitive noun, is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from نبات الأرض; the clause يأكل الناس is a ṣila (relative clause); and الأنعام is conjoined to الناس. (حَتَّى إِذا أَخَذَتِ الْأَرْضُ زُخْرُفَها وَازَّيَّنَتْ): حتى is a particle of limit; إذا is an adverb for the future time, attached to the apodosis, which is أتاها; the clause أخذت is the genitive complement of it; الأرض is the agent; زخرفها is the direct object; and ازينت is conjoined to أخذت. (وَظَنَّ أَهْلُها أَنَّهُمْ قادِرُونَ عَلَيْها): وظن is also a conjoined verb; أهلها is the agent of ظن; أن and what is within its scope fill the place of the two objects of ظن; قادرون is the khabar of أن; and عليها, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to قادرون. (أَتاها أَمْرُنا لَيْلًا أَوْ نَهاراً): أتاها is the apodosis of إذا; the هاء is the direct object; أمرنا is the agent; ليلا is an adverb attached to أتاها; أو is a conjunction; and نهارا is conjoined to ليلا. (فَجَعَلْناها حَصِيداً كَأَنْ لَمْ تَغْنَ بِالْأَمْسِ): The فاء is a conjunction; جعلناها is a verb, agent and first direct object; حصيدا is the second direct object; كأن is the lightened form of the heavy كأنّ, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause لم تغن is its khabar; and بالأمس, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to تغن. By الأمس he meant past time in general, not specifically the day before your own day; for that reason he declined it and attached «ال» to it, whereas had he said أمس, it would have had to be indeclinable on the kasra and stripped of «ال».
(كَذلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ الْآياتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ): كذلك is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); نفصل الآيات is a verb, a latent agent, and a direct object; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to نفصل; and the clause يتفكرون is an adjective of قوم. (وَاللَّهُ يَدْعُوا إِلى دارِ السَّلامِ): والله is a mubtadaʾ; the clause يدعو is the khabar; and إلى دار السلام is attached to يدعو. The difference between دعاء (invitation) and أمر (command) will come in the section on Benefits.
(وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ إِلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ): ويهدي is conjoined to يدعو; من is a direct object; the clause يشاء is a ṣila; إلى صراط is attached to يهدي; and مستقيم is an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
1- In this verse there is a tamthīlī (representational) and composite simile, which here admits of two things:
(a) That He likened the life of this world to water, in the benefit that comes by it and then its cutting off.
(b) That He likened it to vegetation, in its drying up and going away as crumbled stubble after it had been intertwined and thick and had adorned the earth with its greenness and its quivering.
2- In His saying «أخذت الأرض زخرفها» there is an istiʿāra makniyya (implicit metaphor), in that the earth, in its adornment with the varieties of plants upon it, is made like a bride who has taken all kinds of ornaments and garments and adorned herself with them.

* Benefits:
The difference between دعاء and أمر is that the first is the request for an action by that for the sake of which it occurs, and the one who calls to an action is the opposite of the one who turns away from it, and it comes only from the lower to the higher. As for the command, it is an inducement to the action and a rebuke for leaving it, and it requires that the one commanded be lower in rank than the one commanding.

dervis-irab:26-27.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَرْهَقُ) their faces: that is, covers them. الرهق is "covering"; it is said رهقه يرهقه (from the bāb of طرب), that is, "it covered him swiftly", and from it «لا ترهقني من أمري عسرا» and «فلا يخاف بخسا ولا رهقا». One says رهقته and أرهقته like ردفته and أردفته; فعل and أفعل are of one meaning. From it comes أرهقت الصلاة when you delay it until the time of the other prayer covers it, that is, enters. Some said الرهق is "nearness"; from it comes غلام مراهق, a boy who has neared puberty. Others said: الرهق is the reaching of a matter; from it comes راهق الغلام when he joined the men, and رهقه في الحرب, "he overtook him in war". al-Azharī said: الرهق is a noun from الإرهاق, which is that a person be made to bear what he cannot bear; from it comes «سأرهقه صعودا». The letters rāʾ and hāʾ together have a peculiar property: they do not convey one single meaning, but rather convey the producing of an effect. We have counted them, and this constant rule did not fail. So رهيأ الحمل means he made one of the two loads heavier than the other; ترهيأت السحابة means the cloud churned with rain; رهبته means I feared him, and "there is fear of him in my heart", and he is a رجل مرهوب, whose enemy is terrified of him. Laylā said:
وقد كان مرهوب السنان وبيّن الل ... سان ومجذام السّرى غير فاتر
(He was one whose spear-point was feared, clear of tongue, a cutter through night-journeys, not slack.)
And he is a راهب (monk), clearly in his رهبانية (monasticism), and these are رهبان, رهبة, رهابين and رهابنة. A man of the Ḍibāb said:
قد أدبر الليل وقضّى أربه ... وارتفعت في فلكيها الكوكبة
كأنها مصباح دير الرهبة
(The night has turned away and finished its need, and the stars have risen in their orbits, as if they were the lamp of a monastery of monks.)
ورماه فأصاب رهابته: it is a bone in the chest overlooking the belly, like the tip of a dog's tongue. Figuratively: أرهب الإبل عن الحوض, "he drove them away", and أرهب عنه الناس بأسه ونجدته, "his might and courage kept people from him". A man of Jarm said:
إنّا إذا الحرب نساقيها المال ... وجعلت تلقح ثم تحتال
يرهب عنا الناس طعن إيغال ... شزر كأفواه المزاد الشلشال
(When war comes we give it money to drink, and it begins to conceive and then plots; people are kept from us by a deep thrust, slanting, like the mouths of dripping water-skins.)
that is, "we spend money on it". This is from eloquent speech, and what made it eloquent is only the charm of the metaphor. الرهج is dust, and the effect it produces is not hidden; أرهج الغبار means he stirred up the dust, and أرهجت حوافر الخيل. Figuratively: أرهج فلان نار الفتنة بين القوم, "so-and-so stirred up the fire of strife among the people"; "he is devoted to evil, and has turmoil in it". رهز and ارتهز لأمر كذا means he moved for it, was stirred and became eager; نشط here is from الرهز, which is movement in intercourse and otherwise. Among their sayings: "so-and-so is quick to seize on greed and to snatch his opportunities". رهص means he set something right with firmness; when you build a wall, make its رهص firm, which is its lowest course. Figuratively: أرهص الشيء, "he established it and laid its foundation", and "that was an إرهاص (foreshadowing) of prophethood"; ورهصه لامه, "he blamed him", and it is from الرهصة. You say: "No one was mentioned in his presence but he belittled him, and found fault with his leg and trampled him". And "so-and-so is a lion رهيص", meaning he does not leave his place, as if he were pinned down. الرهط is from three to ten, and their effect is plain in gathering together, ordering work and securing victory. al-Walīd ibn ʿUqba, the brother of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, said when ʿUthmān was killed and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib was given the pledge and ordered the seizure of the weapons and the like that were in the house:
بني هاشم إنا وما كان بيننا ... كصدع الصّفا لا يرأب الدهر شاعبه
ثلاثة رهط: قاتلان وسالب ... سواء علينا قاتلاه وسالبه
(O sons of Hāshim, we and what has been between us are like a crack in the rock that its splitter can never mend through time; three groups: two killers and a plunderer; to us his two killers and his plunderer are alike.)
رهف سيفه means its edge became thin, and سيف رهيف and مرهف الحد; رجل مرهف الجسم means slender of body; "you have whetted your tongue against us and sharpened it (أرهفته)". وفيه رهل means swelling. وروضه مرهومة means rained upon. Dhū al-Rumma said:
أو نفحة من أعالي حنوة معجت ... فيها الصّبا موهنا والروض مرهوم
(Or a breath from the heights of Ḥanwa in which the east wind blew in the night's middle, while the meadow was rain-fed.)
الرهن is well known, and the taking of the pledge: الرّهن, الرّهون, الرّهان. واسترهنني فرهنته ضيعتي. Figuratively: جاءا فرسي رهان, two horses of a race, that is, equal; وإني لك رهن بكذا, that is, I am a guarantor for it; ورجلي رهينة, that is, shackled. al-Samhariyy ibn Asad al-ʿUklī said:
لقد طرقت ليلي ورجلي رهينة ... فما راعني في السجن إلا سلامها
(Laylā came by night while my foot was in fetters; in the prison nothing startled me but her greeting.)
وفلان رهن بكذا ورهين ورهينة ومرتهن به: he is held to account for it. The Exalted said «كل امرئ بما كسب رهين» and «كل نفس بما كسبت رهينة». الرهو is stillness. The Exalted said «واترك البحر رهوا», that is, still; and عيش راه is a tranquil life. A bedouin passed by a man who was paralysed and said: "Glory to Allah, stillness between two humps!" One says طلع رهوا ورهوة, which is like a hill. Dhū al-Rumma said:
يجلّي كما جلّى على رأس رهوة ... من الطير أقنى ينفض الطلّ أزرق
(He clears away as a blue, hook-nosed bird clears away, shaking off the dew, on the top of a hillock.)
وجاءت الخيل رهوا means in succession; وأتاه بالشيء رهوا سهوا means easily, without any hindrance. He said:
يمشين رهوا فلا الأعجاز خاذلة ... ولا الصدور على الاعجاز تتكل
(They walk gently, so neither do the rumps fail nor do the chests rely on the rumps.)
This is among the wonders of this noble language.
(القتر): and القترة is dust with blackness in it; one says قتر (as in فرح, نصر and ضرب), and from it is the saying of al-Farazdaq:
متوح برداء الملك يتبعه ... موج ترى فوقه الرايات والقترا
(Clothed in the mantle of kingship, followed by a wave above which you see banners and dust.)
It was also said: القتر is smoke, and from it comes the dust of the cooking pot. It was said: القتر is the small amount, and الاقتار in livelihood is straitness; one says قترت الشيء and اقترته, that is, I reduced it, and from it «وعلى المقتر قدره».
(القطع): the plural of قطعة, of the night, in which there is darkness; and القِطع, with kasra on the qāf and sukūn on the ṭāʾ, is the part of the night in which there is darkness. Both were read.

* I'rab:
(لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا الْحُسْنى وَزِيادَةٌ): للذين is a fronted khabar; the clause أحسنوا is a ṣila; الحسنى is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and زيادة is conjoined to الحسنى, meaning what exceeds the reward. (وَلا يَرْهَقُ وُجُوهَهُمْ قَتَرٌ وَلا ذِلَّةٌ): It is permissible for the wāw to be resumptive, because of the multiplicity of favours to the doers of good, and it is permissible for it to be a conjunction, with the clause يرهق وجوههم conjoined to الحسنى, and then the implying of أن is necessary; so if you wish you put it in the accusative and if you wish you put it in the nominative, in the manner of Maysūn's saying:
ولبس عباءة وتقر عيني ... أحب إليّ من لبس الشفوف
(To wear a cloak and have my eye cooled is dearer to me than wearing fine robes.)
لا is negative; يرهق وجوههم is an imperfect verb and a direct object; قتر is the agent; and ولا ذلة is conjoined to قتر. (أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ): أولئك is a mubtadaʾ; أصحاب is the khabar; الجنة is a muḍāf ilayhi; هم is a mubtadaʾ; فيها is attached to خالدون; and خالدون is the khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl. (وَالَّذِينَ كَسَبُوا السَّيِّئاتِ جَزاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ بِمِثْلِها): It is permissible for the wāw to be a conjunction, with الذين conjoined by sequence to the first الذين, that is, "for those who did good is the best, and for those who earned evil deeds the recompense of an evil deed is the like of it", so that the division is balanced; and this is the easiest of the aspects mentioned by the i'rab-writers and grammarians. It is also permissible for the wāw to be resumptive and الذين a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is جزاء سيئة بمثلها, and this too is an easy view without strain; and there are other views we have set aside because they are strained and there is no need of them. The clause كسبوا السيئات, made of verb, agent and direct object, is the ṣila of the relative; جزاء is a second mubtadaʾ; سيئة is a muḍāf ilayhi; and بمثلها is the khabar of جزاء, that is, an omitted one, "by the like of it". (وَتَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ): It was said that this clause is conjoined to كسبوا, and there is weakness in that on two counts: first, that the future is not conjoined to the past; second, that a long clause intervenes between them. It was said that the wāw is ḥāl and the clause ترهقهم ذلة is a ḥāl, and what is strained in that is not hidden. It was said that the wāw is parenthetical and the clause parenthetical, but a parenthesis is not apt here, because He is enumerating the states of their punishment. We see that the wāw is resumptive and the clause resumptive, as if He were enumerating the kinds of punishment for them to terrify, and likewise His saying: (ما لَهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ عاصِمٍ): ما is negative or Ḥijāzī; لهم is a fronted khabar; من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عاصم; من is redundant; and عاصم is a delayed mubtadaʾ, or the delayed noun of ما according to those who allow the fronting of its khabar. (كَأَنَّما أُغْشِيَتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ قِطَعاً مِنَ اللَّيْلِ مُظْلِماً): This is a resumptive clause that completes the three fates of theirs, namely the equal recompense, the abasement that overtakes them, and the covering of their faces with pieces of the night. كأنما is kāffa and makfūfa; أغشيت is a passive past verb; وجوههم is the nāʾib fāʿil; قطعا is a second direct object; من الليل is an adjective of قطع; and مظلما is a second adjective of قطعا, read with kasra on the qāf and sukūn on the ṭāʾ. On the reading قَطَعاً it is problematic for مظلما to be an adjective, so it is parsed as a ḥāl from الليل, the operator in it being either أغشيت, on the ground that الليل is an adjective of قطعا so that its reaching the described is like its reaching the adjective, or else the sense of the verb in «من الليل». (أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ): This is a fourth resumptive clause in which their inevitable fates are completed; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ, أصحاب النار the khabar, and هم فيها خالدون a nominal clause, a ḥāl from them.

* Benefits:
Ibn Hishām's statement on «والذين كسبوا»:
Ibn Hishām said regarding this verse: The clause «وترهقهم ذلة» is conjoined to «كسبوا السيئات», so it is part of the ṣila, and what lies between them is a parenthesis by which the measure of their recompense is made clear, and the clause «ما لهم من الله من عاصم» is the khabar; so said Ibn ʿUṣfūr, and it is far-fetched, because the apparent sense is that «ترهقهم» was not brought in to define «الذين» so as to be conjoined to its ṣila, but was brought to announce what befalls them as recompense for their earning evil deeds. Further, it is not determinate, since it is possible that the khabar is «جزاء سيئة بمثلها», in which case there is no parenthesis in the verse; and it is possible that the khabar is the negative clause as mentioned, with the two clauses before it parenthetical; or that the khabar is «كأنما أغشيت», so that the parenthesis is of three clauses; or «أولئك أصحاب النار», so that the parenthesis is of four clauses. It is also possible, and this is the most apparent, that «الذين» is not a mubtadaʾ but is conjoined to the first «الذين», that is, «للذين أحسنوا الحسنى وزيادة» and for those who earned evil deeds the recompense of an evil deed is the like of it; so "its like" here is set against "the increase" there. Its parallel in meaning is the saying of the Exalted «من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها ومن جاء بالسيئة فلا يجزى الذين عملوا السيئات إلا ما كانوا يعملون», and in wording their saying "In the house is Zayd and in the room ʿAmr", which is conjoining upon the two governed items of two different operators according to al-Akhfash, and upon the implying of the preposition according to Sībawayh and the verifiers. Among the things that favour this aspect is that the apparent sense is that the bāʾ in «بمثلها» is attached to الجزاء; so if «جزاء سيئة» is a mubtadaʾ, a khabar has to be implied, that is "occurring", as Abū al-Baqāʾ said, or «لهم», as al-Ḥūfī said, and that is better because it dispenses with implying a link between this clause and its mubtadaʾ, which is الذين. According to what we have chosen, «جزاء» is conjoined to «الحسنى», so no other implication is needed. As for the saying of Abū al-Ḥasan and Kaysān that «بمثلها» is the khabar and that the bāʾ was added in the khabar as it is added in the mubtadaʾ in «بحسبك درهم», it is rejected by the majority; yet their view may be supported by His saying «وجزاء سيئة سيئة».

dervis-irab:28-30.t:
* Vocabulary:
(زيلنا): we separated.
(تَبْلُوا): you test.

* I'rab:
(وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعاً): The adverb is attached to an omitted element understood from the preceding verse, that is, "We do all that on the day We gather them"; the clause نحشرهم is the genitive complement of it; and جميعا is accusative as a ḥāl. (ثُمَّ نَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا مَكانَكُمْ أَنْتُمْ وَشُرَكاؤُكُمْ): ثم is a particle of conjunction and delay; نقول is conjoined to what the adverb is attached to, that is, "We do all that, then We say", or it is conjoined to نحشرها; للذين is attached to نقول; the clause أشركوا is a ṣila; مكانكم is an ism fiʿl amr (command-verb noun) meaning "Keep to"; its discussion will come in the section on Benefits; أنتم is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative, an emphasis (tawkīd) of the pronoun in مكانكم; and شركاؤكم is conjoined to it. (فَزَيَّلْنا بَيْنَهُمْ وَقالَ شُرَكاؤُهُمْ ما كُنْتُمْ إِيَّانا تَعْبُدُونَ): The فاء is resumptive; زيلنا is a verb and agent; بينهم is an adverb attached to زيلنا; قال شركاؤهم is a verb and agent; ما is negative; كنتم is kāna and its noun; إيانا is a detached pronoun, a fronted direct object of تعبدون; and the clause تعبدون is accusative, the khabar of كنتم. (فَكَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيداً بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَكُمْ): The فاء is resumptive; كفى is a past verb; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; الله is the agent in position; and as for شهيدا, al-Zajjāj said it is accusative as tamyīz if you wish and as ḥāl if you wish; if the noun is inert, the accusative is tamyīz, as in the saying of Bashshār:
ومن ذا الذي ترضى سجاياه كلها ... كفى بالمرء نبلا أن تعدّ معايبه
(And who is it whose every trait is pleasing? It suffices a man as nobility that his faults can be counted.)
(إِنْ كُنَّا عَنْ عِبادَتِكُمْ لَغافِلِينَ): إن is the lightened form of the heavy إنّ and is not negative, as one of the imams said; it is inoperative, as already mentioned; كنا is kāna and its noun; عن عبادتكم is attached to غافلين; the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), which is what removed the negative إن; and غافلين is the khabar of كنا. (هُنالِكَ تَبْلُوا كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ما أَسْلَفَتْ): هنالك is a demonstrative in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, attached to تبلو; the lām is for distance and the kāf for address; تبلو كل نفس is an imperfect verb and agent; ما is a relative noun, a direct object; and the clause أسلفت is a ṣila. (وَرُدُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ مَوْلاهُمُ الْحَقِّ): The wāw is a conjunction; ردوا is a passive past verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; إلى الله, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to ردوا; مولاهم is an adjective or a badal of الله; and الحق is an adjective, because they used to take as patrons that which has no reality in lordship. (وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ): وضل: the wāw is a conjunction, and ضل is conjoined to ردوا; عنهم is attached to ضل; ما is a relative noun, the agent; كانوا is kāna and its noun; the clause كانوا يفترون is a ṣila; and the clause يفترون is the khabar of كانوا.

* Benefits:
(مَكانَكُمْ): a word that has come to run in the manner of a threat; the Arabs threaten and say "Your place!" and "Wait for me". The sound view according to the verifiers is that مكانك and دونك are among the asmāʾ al-afʿāl (verb-nouns). We say that the verb-nouns are of two kinds, the coined (murtajal) and the transferred (manqūl). The coined are those which were put from the first as verb-nouns, and they are three kinds: a past verb-noun such as هيهات, an imperfect verb-noun such as أف, and an imperative verb-noun such as آمين, as has already been indicated. The transferred are those used for something other than a verb-noun and then transferred to it, and the transfer is:
1- either from a preposition and its genitive noun, such as عليك نفسك, that is, "keep to it", and إليك عني, that is, "stand aside";
2- or from an adverb, such as دونك الكتاب, that is, "take it", and مكانك, which has already been mentioned;
3- or from a maṣdar, such as رويد أخاك, that is, "give him time", and بله الشر, that is, "leave it and abandon it";
4- or from an interjection, such as ها الكتاب, that is, "take it", and «هاؤم اقرءوا كتابيه»;
5- or by deviation (maʿdūla), such as نزال and حذار.
Notes:
1- The kāf attached to the transferred verb-noun varies according to the one addressed in singular, dual, plural, masculine and feminine; it is a particle of address with no grammatical position, because it is like a part of the word that has no i'rab.
2- The transferred and the deviated verb-noun comes only for the command and not for anything else, unlike the coined, as already mentioned.
3- The coined and the transferred are samāʿī (based on usage) and are not subject to analogy.
4- The deviated is qiyāsī (subject to analogy) and is built on the pattern فعال from every triliteral, bare, complete, inflecting verb.
More on this will come in the course of this book.

dervis-irab:62-65.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الولي) is the opposite of the enemy; so he is the one who loves. The servants' love of Allah is their obedience to Him, and His love of them is His honouring them. On the first sense, فعيل has the meaning of fāʿil (active); on the second, the meaning of mafʿūl (passive); so it is shared between the two. Now we have investigated all the compounds in the words whose first, middle and last radicals are wāw, and whose last radical is lām and yāʾ, and we found that they come down to a meaning of nearness and proximity. One says: وليه وليا: he came near to him; and أوليته إياه: I brought him near to it; "eat of what is next to you" (كل مما يليك) and "I sat next to him" (جلست مما يليه); and سقط الوليّ, which is the rain that follows the first spring rain (al-wasmī); وليت الأرض, and it is "ruled over" (مولّية); ولي الأمر and تولاه, and he is its guardian (waliyyuhu) and master (mawlāhu); he is the guardian of the orphan and the guardian of the slain man, and they are his guardians (awliyāʾuhu); ولي ولاية; and he is the governor (wālī) of the town and they are its governors (wulāt); "may Allah have mercy on the just governors"; واستولى عليه; and "this is my mawlā": my cousin, and "they are my mawālī"; and "my mawlā": my master and my slave; and a mawlā of clear authority is a master and helper, and he is more entitled to it (awlā bihi); ووالاه موالاة; and ووالى between two things, and they are in succession (walāʾ). The Arabs say: "separate your sheep from my sheep" (wāli ghanamaka min ghanamī), i.e. set them apart and distinguish them; and if the sheep are both ewes and goats it is said "separate them". Dhū al-Rumma said:
يوالي إذا اصطكّ الخصوم أمامه ... وجوه القضايا من وجوه المظالم
(He distinguishes, when the litigants clash before him, the aspects of the cases from the aspects of wrongs.)
وولاه ركنه: he turned his side to him. «فولّ وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام» (so turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque); and تواليته: I made him a guardian: «ومن يتولهم منكم فإنه منهم» (and whoever among you takes them as allies, then he is of them); and تولاك الله بحفظه (may Allah take you under His protection); and he put the wilīya on the riding-beast, which is the packsaddle. Abū Zubayd said: كالبلايا رؤسها في الولايا ... ما نحات السّموم حرّ الخدود (like the camels left to die at graves, their heads on the saddle-cloths, whom the hot winds have stripped of the heat of their cheeks). And ولّى عني and تولى, and «أولى لك» (woe to you), meaning ويل لك; and استولى على الغاية. This is from the rare in the highest degree.
[Translator's note: the second verse by Abū Zubayd is given in the source without a verse break and the gloss is tentative; I translated the text as printed.]

* I'rab:
(أَلا إِنَّ أَوْلِياءَ اللَّهِ لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ) ألا is a particle of alerting (tanbīh) with which speech is opened, composed of the hamza and the negative لا, changed from its first meaning to alerting. وإن أولياء الله: inna and its noun; لا is negative; خوف is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and it was permissible to begin with it because of its negation; عليهم is the khabar (predicate) of لا [sic]; ولا: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negative; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يحزنون is its khabar.
(الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَكانُوا يَتَّقُونَ) The position of الذين آمنوا admits three equally preferable possibilities. First, the accusative, as an adjective of أولياء الله. Second, the nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. هم الذين آمنوا. Third, the nominative as mubtadaʾ, with the khabar being the following clause لهم البشرى. The clause آمنوا is a ṣila (relative clause); وكانوا يتقون is conjoined to the ṣila; and the clause يتقون is the khabar of كانوا.
َهُمُ الْبُشْرى فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا)
[Translator's note: the opening of this Qur'anic quotation is truncated in the source, which reads «َهُمُ الْبُشْرى»; the verse is لَهُمُ الْبُشْرى فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا.]
لهم is a fronted khabar and البشرى a delayed mubtadaʾ; في الحياة is attached to an omitted word, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of البشرى, the operator in the ḥāl being the settling (istiqrār) implied in لهم; and الدنيا is an adjective of الحياة. The clause لهم البشرى is either resumptive; and if الذين is made a mubtadaʾ, it is in the position of the nominative as khabar.
َ فِي الْآخِرَةِ لا تَبْدِيلَ لِكَلِماتِ اللَّهِ)
[Translator's note: the opening of the quotation is truncated in the source; the text is وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ.]
وفي الآخرة is conjoined to في الحياة الدنيا; لا is the lā of generic negation, تبديل is its noun, and لكلمات الله is the khabar of لا.
لِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ)
[Translator's note: the opening is truncated in the source; the text is ذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ.]
ذلك is a mubtadaʾ; هو is a second mubtadaʾ; الفوز is the khabar of هو, and the clause is the khabar of ذلك; العظيم is an adjective of الفوز; and the two clauses are parenthetical (muʿtariḍatān). (وَلا يَحْزُنْكَ قَوْلُهُمْ إِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعاً هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; يحزنك is an imperfect verb jussive (majzūm) by لا, and the kāf is a direct object; قولهم is the agent; and إن and its noun. Its hamza takes kasra because the sentence is resumptive in the sense of giving a reason for the might of Allah; and it is not permissible that it takes kasra because it occurs after قول, because it would then become a quotation from them, and the Prophet ﷺ would have been grieved by that, which would be disbelief. ولله is the khabar of إن; جميعا is a ḥāl of العزة, and it may be an emphasis (tawkīd); it is not feminized with tāʾ because فعيل is the same for masculine and feminine. هو is a mubtadaʾ; السميع is its first khabar and العليم its second khabar.

dervis-irab:66-67.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَخْرُصُونَ) The original sense of الخرص is estimation (ḥazr), i.e. conjecture and assessment, and it is used for lying because that is how it is predominantly used. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "I estimated the palm-trees, khaṣtu al-nakhla kharṣan, of the pattern qatala: I estimated its fruit, and the noun is al-khirṣ with kasra. And khaṣa al-kāfir kharṣan: he lied; so he is a khāriṣ and a kharrāṣ."
[Translator's note: the source prints خرصت/خرص and the verbal form as written; I translated it as printed.]

* I'rab:
(أَلا إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ) ألا is a particle of alerting, which has been mentioned; إن is a particle resembling the verb; ولله is its fronted khabar (predicate); and من is its delayed noun. He singled out those with intellect for mention in order to magnify: for if they belong to Him and are included in His dominion, then what lies beyond them, that which has no intellect, is all the more not to have any peer or partner. في السموات is the ṣila (relative clause) of من, and ومن في الأرض is conjoined to من في السموات.
(وَما يَتَّبِعُ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ شُرَكاءَ) ما is negative; يتبع الذين is an imperfect verb and an agent; the clause يدعون is a ṣila; and من دون الله is a ḥāl of شركاء because it precedes it; شركاء is the direct object of يتبع, and the object of يدعون is omitted because the meaning is understood. The implied form is: "those who invoke other than Allah, gods as partners, do not follow", i.e. they do not follow in reality the partners, even if they call them partners, because partnership with Allah in lordship is impossible: ﴿إن يتبعون إلا ظنهم﴾ that they are partners. It is also possible that ما is interrogative, and is then accusative by what follows it, i.e. "what do they follow?"; Abū al-Baqāʾ inclined to this i'rab. It is also possible that ما is a relative noun conjoined to من, as though He says: "By Allah, whatever those who invoke partners besides Allah follow" is His, i.e. "and His are their partners". It is also possible that this relative ما is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ with an omitted khabar, its implied form being: "and that which the polytheists follow is falsehood". These are four possibilities which we have given because they are close in preference, though the first is the easiest of them.
(إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَخْرُصُونَ) إن is negative; يتبعون is a verb and an agent; إلا is a particle of restriction; الظن is a direct object; and إن is also negative; هم is a mubtadaʾ; إلا is a particle of restriction; and the clause يخرصون is their khabar.
(هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ لِتَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ وَالنَّهارَ مُبْصِراً) هو is a mubtadaʾ and الذي is the khabar; the clause جعل is the ṣila of the relative. Then, if الجعل means origination and creation, it takes one object; if it means making into (taṣyīr), it takes two objects. In either case لكم is attached to جعل and الليل is a direct object. لتسكنوا: the lām is for reason, and تسكنوا is accusative by an implied أن; the preposition and its genitive noun is either an object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi) or a second direct object; فيه is attached to تسكنوا; النهار is conjoined to الليل; and مبصرا is either a ḥāl or a second direct object, as already stated. (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَسْمَعُونَ) إن is a particle resembling the verb; وفي ذلك is the fronted khabar of إن; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آيات is the delayed noun of إن; لقوم is an adjective of آيات; and the clause يسمعون is an adjective of القوم.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «والنهار مبصرا» there is a rational figurative expression (majāz ʿaqlī), for the attribution of seeing to the day is not literal. It has already been said that the rational figure is the attribution of an action or its like to something other than that to which it belongs, as in the saying of Abū Tammām:
تكاد عطاياه يجنّ جنونها ... إذا لم يعوذها بنغمة طالب
(His gifts are almost driven mad, if he does not shield them with the plea of a petitioner.)
It may also be treated as an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya) if comparison is intended. Of this is the saying of Jarīr:
لقد لمتنا يا أم غالب في السّرى ... ونمت وما ليل المطيّ بنائم
(You blamed us, Umm Ghālib, for the night journey, and you slept, while the night of the riding-beasts does not sleep.)

dervis-irab:31-33.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ مَنْ يَرْزُقُكُمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ): من is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ; the clause يرزقكم is the khabar; من السماء, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to يرزقكم; and الأرض is conjoined. (أَمَّنْ يَمْلِكُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصارَ): أم is a conjunction, and it is munqaṭiʿa (disconnected), because it is not preceded by the interrogative hamza nor by a statement of equivalence; من is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ; the clause يملك is the khabar; السمع is a direct object; and الأبصار is conjoined to السمع. (وَمَنْ يُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ وَيُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتَ مِنَ الْحَيِّ وَمَنْ يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ): also a conjunction, and what follows it is conjoined. (فَسَيَقُولُونَ اللَّهُ): The فاء is resumptive; يقولون is a verb and agent; and الله is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "He is Allah", or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being "does all these things"; and the clause is the content of the saying. (فَقُلْ أَفَلا تَتَّقُونَ): The فاء is the fāʾ faṣīḥa (eloquent fāʾ); قل is an imperative verb; the hamza is interrogative; the فاء is a conjunction; لا is negative; and تتقون is an imperfect verb and agent. (فَذلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمُ الْحَقُّ): The فاء is a conjunction; ذلكم is a mubtadaʾ; الله is the khabar; ربكم is a badal of الله or an adjective; and الحق is an adjective of ربكم. It is also permissible to parse الله as a second mubtadaʾ and ربكم as its khabar, the clause being the khabar of the demonstrative. (فَماذا بَعْدَ الْحَقِّ إِلَّا الضَّلالُ فَأَنَّى تُصْرَفُونَ): The فاء is a conjunction; as for ماذا, it was previously mentioned that there are two aspects: the first, that all of it is one noun because of their composition, the interrogative prevailing over the demonstrative, the sense of the interrogative here becoming negation, which is why إلا follows it, and it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the second, that ذا is a relative, the khabar of the interrogative ما, with بعد an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl, and إلا a particle of restriction, and الضلال a badal of ذا, the interrogative being in the sense of negation here too. The فاء is a conjunction; أنى is an interrogative noun meaning كيف, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of تصرفون; and تصرفون is a passive imperfect verb with a nāʾib fāʿil. (كَذلِكَ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ فَسَقُوا أَنَّهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ):
The kāf is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, and the pointing with ذلك is to the maṣdar understood, that is, "like their being turned away from the truth after acknowledging it in His saying «فسيقولون الله»", or the pointing is to the truth. حقت كلمة ربك is a verb and agent; على الذين, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to حقت; the clause فسقوا is a ṣila; and أن and what is within its scope is a badal of كلمة ربك, that is, "it is fitting for them that they do not believe"; and the clause لا يؤمنون is the khabar of أن.

dervis-irab:34-36.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ هَلْ مِنْ شُرَكائِكُمْ مَنْ يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ): هل is a particle of interrogation; من شركائهم is a fronted khabar; من is a relative, a delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause يبدأ الخلق is a ṣila; and ثم is a particle conjoining to يبدأ. [Translator's note: the source writes «شركائهم» (their partners) here, while the verse reads «شركائكم»; translated as written.] (قُلِ اللَّهُ يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ فَأَنَّى تُؤْفَكُونَ): الله is a mubtadaʾ; the clause يبدأ الخلق is its khabar; the nominal clause is the content of the saying; ثم يعيده is conjoined to يبدأ; the فاء is a conjunction; أنى is an interrogative noun meaning كيف, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; and تؤفكون is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil. (قُلْ هَلْ مِنْ شُرَكائِكُمْ مَنْ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ): another argument against what was mentioned; من شركائكم is a fronted khabar; من is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and يهدي is an imperfect verb that takes two objects, the second being introduced either by the lām or by إلى, and the preposition is sometimes omitted for lightness. In this verse the two modes of transitivity by a preposition are combined: the first and the third are made transitive by إلى and the second by the lām, and the first direct object of the three verbs is omitted. The implied form is: "Is there among your partners one who guides another to the truth? Say: Allah guides whom He wills to the truth. Is then he who guides another to the truth...?" The secret in the variation of the prepositions will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(قُلِ اللَّهُ يَهْدِي لِلْحَقِّ): the i'rab of its like has gone before. (أَفَمَنْ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ أَحَقُّ أَنْ يُتَّبَعَ): The hamza is for denying interrogation, and it is the eighth question whose answer is not mentioned, and the answer here is "Allah"; من is a mubtadaʾ and أحق its khabar; أن is a maṣdar and accusative-governing particle; يتبع is passive; and the interpreted maṣdar is a muḍāf ilayhi of أحق after being put in the accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "more deserving of being followed". (أَمَّنْ لا يَهِدِّي إِلَّا أَنْ يُهْدى): أم is a conjunction; من is a mubtadaʾ; the clause لا يهدي is a ṣila; إلا is a particle of restriction; أن and what is within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, so the exception is "emptied" (mufarragh) of the most general of states, that is, "he does not guide or become guided in any state except the state of his being guided", i.e. of others guiding him; and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "more deserving". You may also make من conjoined to the first من, in which case you do not need the khabar. (فَما لَكُمْ كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ): The فاء is resumptive; ما is interrogative, a mubtadaʾ; and لكم is its khabar, that is, "what thing is established for you in taking these, who are unable to guide themselves, so how do you judge with falsehood and set up rivals and partners to Allah?" (وَما يَتَّبِعُ أَكْثَرُهُمْ إِلَّا ظَنًّا): a resumptive speech conveyed to explain the secret of their not grasping the truth and not understanding the content of the proof; ما is negative; يتبع أكثرهم is a verb and agent; إلا is a particle of restriction; and ظنا is a direct object. (إِنَّ الظَّنَّ لا يُغْنِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ شَيْئاً): a resumptive speech conveyed to explain the reason for their failing to understand and not grasping it; إن and its noun, with the clause لا يغني as its khabar; من الحق is a fronted ḥāl; and شيئا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, that is, "any bit of avail", or a direct object by including in يغني the sense of "repels". (إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِما يَفْعَلُونَ): إن with its noun and khabar; بما is attached to عليم; and the clause يفعلون has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila of ما, whether it be relative or maṣdar.

* Rhetoric:
The variation of prepositions:
This is a topic to which reference was made earlier in al-Anfāl, and it contains the secret of the variation of prepositions. Most people put these particles in the wrong places and are ignorant of the subtleties hidden in their placement where they are placed. Here the verb هدى is made transitive to «الحق» by إلى twice, and in the third by the lām. The grammarians are heedless of this secret and say that whatever may be governed by إلى may be governed by the lām, which gives the sense of limit as it does, but not conversely; so one does not say, for "I said to him" (قلت له), "قلت اليه"; and they say "the water is in the cup" because في is for containment, and they allow transitivity by الباء because it takes its place in containment, and it is not permitted to say, for "I passed by him" (مررت به), "مررت فيه". Once this is established we say, and Allah knows best, that there is a secret behind the form. When guidance is attributed to them, it must be made transitive by إلى, which conveys distance, as though it were by implication far from them; but when it is attributed to Allah the Exalted, it must be made transitive by the lām, which conveys nearness, as though it were among His exclusive attributes and the possession of His right hand, He alone having it in a manner of permanence and perfection. Lofty examples of this variation will come.

dervis-irab:37-40.t:
* I'rab:
(وَما كانَ هذَا الْقُرْآنُ أَنْ يُفْتَرى مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ): The wāw is resumptive; ما is negative; كان with its noun; القرآن is a badal of هذا; and أن and what is within its scope is the khabar of كان, that is, "a fabrication". (وَلكِنْ تَصْدِيقَ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ): The wāw is a conjunction; لكن is the lightened, inoperative one; تصديق is conjoined to the interpreted افتراء; and لكن has fallen in the best of places because it is between two opposites, falsehood and truth, so there is no need for the aspects strained by some imams, which are acceptable and admissible, but what we have given is preferable to put first. الذي is a muḍāf ilayhi of تصديق; بين is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative; and يديه is a muḍāf ilayhi of بين, meaning "before it". (وَتَفْصِيلَ الْكِتابِ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ): تفصيل is conjoined to تصديق; لا is the lā of generic negation; ريب is its noun, indeclinable on the fatḥa; فيه is the khabar of لا; من رب العالمين is a ḥāl; and the clause لا ريب فيه is parenthetical, and that is the apparent sense, between تفصيل and من رب العالمين, the implied form being: "but confirmation of what is before it and an exposition of the Book, being from the Lord of the worlds". al-Zamakhsharī leaned toward making لا ريب فيه a ḥāl falling within the scope of the istidrāk (rectification), as if it were said: "but it was a confirmation and an exposition, doubt being negated from it, being from the Lord of the worlds". You may also attach من رب العالمين to تفصيلا, in which case لا ريب فيه is parenthetical.
(أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ): أم is a disconnected conjunction, so it means بل, so much so that a rare reading came with it; so it is for transitional iḍrāb (turning away). The hamza is for denying interrogation, of what has occurred and finding it improbable. It is also possible that it be connected (muttaṣila), and then a clause must be omitted so that the balance is sound, the implied form being "Do they acknowledge it, or do they say 'He has fabricated it'?" The clause افتراه is the content of the saying. (قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِسُورَةٍ مِثْلِهِ): The فاء is the fāʾ faṣīḥa, that is, "Say, to reproach them: if the matter is as you say, then bring"; أتوا is an imperative verb and agent; بسورة, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to ائتوا; and مثله is an adjective. (وَادْعُوا مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): وادعوا is conjoined to فأتوا and the wāw is the agent; من is a relative noun, a direct object; the clause استطعتم is a ṣila; من دون الله is a ḥāl; إن is conditional; كنتم is the protasis, the tāʾ being the noun of كان; صادقين is the khabar of كان; and the apodosis is omitted, that is, "then bring and call". (بَلْ كَذَّبُوا بِما لَمْ يُحِيطُوا بِعِلْمِهِ وَلَمَّا يَأْتِهِمْ تَأْوِيلُهُ): بل is a particle of iḍrāb and conjunction; كذبوا is a verb and agent; بما is attached to كذبوا; the clause لم يحيطوا is the ṣila of ما; and the wāw is for ḥāl. It is also possible that it be a conjunction, that is, "rather they denied what they did not encompass in knowledge, and what its interpretation had not come to them", or this clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, that is, "they denied it while they had not understood what they denied nor had their minds reached it". لما is a particle of jussive; يأتهم is an imperfect verb jussive by لما, and the هاء is a direct object; and تأويله is the agent of يأتهم. It is also possible that the wāw is for conjunction and the clause conjoined to لم يحيطوا, thus entering the ruling of the ṣila; and in the coming of «ما» there is a secret on which you will stand in the section on Rhetoric. (كَذلِكَ كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الظَّالِمِينَ): The kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "with such denial those before them denied their messengers"; كذب الذين is a verb and agent; من قبلهم is the ṣila of الذين; فانظر: the فاء is conjoined to an omitted element, that is, "so We destroyed them, so look"; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كان, and the verb فانظر cannot act upon it, because what precedes the interrogative does not act upon it; عاقبة is its noun and الظالمين a muḍāf ilayhi. (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ لا يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ وَرَبُّكَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُفْسِدِينَ): ومنهم is a fronted khabar; من is a delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause يؤمن به is a ṣila; the clause ومنهم من لا يؤمن is conjoined to the preceding clause; ربك is a mubtadaʾ; أعلم is the khabar; and بالمفسدين, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to أعلم.

* Rhetoric:
In «لما» in His saying the Exalted «بل كذبوا بما لم يحيطوا بعلمه ولما يأتهم تأويله» there is a wonderful secret. It gives the speech a meaning that could not have been had it not entered, because it conveys expectation after the negation of encompassing its knowledge. It has given the following:
1- That they denied on the spur of the moment before they pondered it and reached its depths.
2- Insistence on blind imitation and following their fathers, who were bred to obstinacy, sophistry and denial of the truth despite its manifestness and clarity.
3- That denial before encompassing knowledge might suggest an excuse for them, so the word «لما» came decisive, indicating that they had surely encompassed its knowledge, cutting off their arguments and confirming their wretchedness.

dervis-irab:68-70.t:
* I'rab:
(قالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَداً سُبْحانَهُ) قالوا is a verb and an agent; اتخذ الله ولدا is a verb, an agent and a direct object, and the clause is the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); سبحانه is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) of an omitted verb.
(هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ) هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and الغني is its khabar (predicate); وله is a fronted khabar; ما is a delayed mubtadaʾ; في السموات is a ṣila (relative clause); and ما في الأرض is conjoined to ما في السموات.
(إِنْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ سُلْطانٍ بِهذا) إن is negative; عندكم is an adverbial attached to an omitted word, a fronted khabar; من is a redundant preposition; سلطان is a delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative in position and genitive in form; and بهذا is an adjective of سلطان. (أَتَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ) The hamza is for denunciatory interrogation; تقولون is an imperfect verb and an agent; على الله is attached to تقولون; ما is a direct object; and the clause لا تعلمون is a ṣila.
(قُلْ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ لا يُفْلِحُونَ) قل is an imperative verb whose agent is "you"; إن الذين: inna and its noun; the clause يفترون is the ṣila of الذين; على الله is attached to يفترون; الكذب is a direct object; and the clause لا يفلحون is the khabar of إن.
(مَتاعٌ فِي الدُّنْيا ثُمَّ إِلَيْنا مَرْجِعُهُمْ ثُمَّ نُذِيقُهُمُ الْعَذابَ الشَّدِيدَ بِما كانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ) متاع is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. ذاك or هو; في الدنيا is an adjective. It is also possible that متاع is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being "they have enjoyment", and it was permissible to begin with it because of its qualification. ثم is a conjunction implying delay; إلينا is a fronted khabar and مرجعهم a delayed mubtadaʾ; ثم is likewise a conjunction; نذيقهم is a verb, a latent agent and a first direct object; العذاب is a second direct object; الشديد is an adjective; بما: the bāʾ is a preposition of causation and ما is maṣdarī (verbal), i.e. "because of their disbelieving"; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to نذيقهم.

dervis-irab:71-73.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَأَجْمِعُوا) One says: أجمع الأمر and أزمعه when he intended it and resolved upon it. Al-Muʾarrij said: "أجمعت الأمر is more eloquent than أجمعت عليه." Abū al-Haytham said: "أجمع أمره when he made it a unity (jamʿ) after it had been scattered." (الغمة) is the narrowness of a matter, from غمة when he covered it; of this is his saying (peace and blessings be upon him): «ولا غمة في فرائض الله» (and there is no obscurity in the obligations of Allah). And غم الهلال when clouds come between and veil its sighting.

* I'rab:
(وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ نُوحٍ إِذْ قالَ لِقَوْمِهِ) واتل is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) with the omission of the weak letter, and its agent is "you"; عليهم is attached to اتل; نبأ is a direct object; نوح is a muḍāf ilayhi; إذ is an adverbial for the past, in the position of the accusative as a substitute (badal) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) for نبأ, or attached to it. There is no sense in the statement of Abū al-Baqāʾ that it is a ḥāl of نبأ, just as it is not permissible to attach it to the verb, which is اتل, because the meaning would be invalid: اتل is future and the adverbial is past. The clause قال لقومه is added to the adverbial. (يا قَوْمِ إِنْ كانَ كَبُرَ عَلَيْكُمْ مَقامِي وَتَذْكِيرِي بِآياتِ اللَّهِ فَعَلَى اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ) يا is a vocative particle and قوم is the one addressed (munādā), added to the omitted yāʾ of the first person, a matter already discussed; إن is conditional; كان is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause كبر عليكم مقامي is its khabar. What is meant by the "greatness of the standing" is the weightiness of the burden. المقام with fatḥa is rank and station; the Exalted said: «ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان» (and for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens). And المقام with ḍamma is dwelling and persevering in the call during the period of stay, since he remained among them a thousand years less fifty. وتذكيري is conjoined to مقامي; بآيات الله is attached to تذكيري; فعلى الله: the fāʾ is a connector (rābiṭa) and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to توكلت.
(فَأَجْمِعُوا أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكاءَكُمْ) The fāʾ is the eloquent (faṣīḥa) fāʾ; أجمعوا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the agent; أمركم is a direct object, because it is transitive by itself and by a preposition, as stated in the Vocabulary section. وشركاءكم: the wāw is for accompaniment and شركاءكم is an object of accompaniment (mafʿūl maʿahu); Sībawayh stated this explicitly and cited:
فكونوا أنتم وبني أبيكم ... مكان الكليتين من الطحال
(Be, you and the sons of your father, in the place of the two kidneys from the spleen.)
Al-Naḥḥās said: there are three possibilities for the accusative of الشركاء on the reading of the majority:
First: the meaning is وادعوا شركاءكم ("and call your partners"), said by al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, i.e. call them to help you; on this it is accusative by an implied verb.
Second: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd al-Mubarrad said: it is conjoined according to the meaning, as the poet said:
يا ليت زوجك في الوغى ... متقلدا سيفا ورمحا
(Would that your husband were in the battle, girded with a sword and a spear.)
The spear is not girded with, but it is carried over like the sword.
Third: al-Zajjāj said: the meaning is "with your partners", so the wāw on this is the wāw of accompaniment. As for the reading فاجمعوا with a hamzat waṣl, the conjunction is evident, i.e. "gather your matter and gather your partners". As for directing the nominative reading, it is by conjoining الشركاء to the nominative pronoun in أجمعوا, and this conjunction is good even without emphasis by a detached pronoun, as is the requirement in that.
(ثُمَّ لا يَكُنْ أَمْرُكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ غُمَّةً) ثم is a conjunction implying delay; لا is prohibitive; يكن is jussive by لا; أمركم is the noun of يكن; عليكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial) because it was originally an adjective and was fronted; and غمة is the khabar of يكن. (ثُمَّ اقْضُوا إِلَيَّ وَلا تُنْظِرُونِ) ثم is a conjunction, as stated; اقضوا is an imperative verb and an agent; إلي is attached to it; ولا: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is prohibitive; تنظرون was originally تنظرونني, jussive by لا, the nūn being dropped for the jussive and the yāʾ of the first person dropped for the verse-endings (fawāṣil), i.e. "do not give me respite".
(فَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَما سَأَلْتُكُمْ مِنْ أَجْرٍ) The fāʾ is resumptive; إن is conditional; توليتم is a verb and an agent, in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the fāʾ is a connector; ما is negative; سألتكم is a verb and an agent; من is redundant; and أجر is a direct object in position.
(إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى اللَّهِ وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ) إن is negative; أجري is a mubtadaʾ; إلا is a particle of restriction; على الله is the khabar. وأمرت: the wāw is a conjunction; أمرت is a passive past verb and the tāʾ is a nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). وأن أكون: أن and what is in its domain are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. بأن أكون.
(فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَنَجَّيْناهُ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ فِي الْفُلْكِ وَجَعَلْناهُمْ خَلائِفَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction to what precedes; كذبوه is a verb, an agent and a direct object; فنجيناه is conjoined to كذبوه; ومن is a relative noun conjoined to the hāʾ; the adverbial is attached to an omitted word that is the ṣila, i.e. "they settled with him in the ship"; في الفلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نجيناه, or to the settling that is the ṣila, i.e. "and those who settled with him in the ship"; وجعلناهم خلائف is a verb, an agent and its two objects. (وَأَغْرَقْنَا الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا) وأغرقنا is conjoined to نجيناه; نا is the agent; الذين is a direct object; the clause كذبوا بآياتنا is a ṣila; and بآياتنا is attached to كذبوا. (فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; انظر is an imperative verb with a latent agent; كيف is an interrogative noun, a fronted khabar of كان; عاقبة is its noun; and المنذرين is a muḍāf ilayhi.

* Rhetoric:
1- A rational figurative expression (majāz ʿaqlī) in His saying «كبر عليكم مقامي»: greatness has been attributed to the standing (maqām), and the standing is a metonymy for the self, because place is among its concomitants.
2- An implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya) in His saying «ثم اقضوا إلي», i.e. carry out that matter, or discharge it to me. The omitted matter is likened to a debt; then the thing likened to is omitted and one of its properties is taken, namely settling (qaḍāʾ); one says "so-and-so settled his debt", i.e. paid it.

dervis-irab:74-78.t:
* I'rab:
(ثُمَّ بَعَثْنا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ رُسُلًا إِلى قَوْمِهِمْ) It is conjoined to the story of Nūḥ. بعثنا is a verb and an agent; من بعده is a ḥāl; رسلا is a direct object; and إلى قومهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective. (فَجاؤُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ فَما كانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا بِما كَذَّبُوا بِهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ)
The fāʾ is a conjunction; جاءوهم is a verb, an agent and a direct object; بالبينات is attached to جاءوهم; the fāʾ is a conjunction; ما is negative; كان and its noun; the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); يؤمنوا is accusative by an implied أن after it; the lām and what it governs are the khabar of كان; بما is attached to يؤمنوا; the clause كذبوا is a ṣila; به is attached to كذبوا; and من قبل is a ḥāl, with قبل built on ḍamma because it is cut off from the genitive construct in form but not in meaning. (كَذلِكَ نَطْبَعُ عَلى قُلُوبِ الْمُعْتَدِينَ) The kāf is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "we seal with a sealing like that sealing"; and على قلوب المعتدين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نطبع. (ثُمَّ بَعَثْنا مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ مُوسى وَهارُونَ إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَائِهِ بِآياتِنا) This too joins a story to a story, as a case of conjoining the specific to the general. من بعدهم is a ḥāl; موسى is the direct object of بعثنا; هارون is conjoined to موسى; إلى فرعون is attached to بعثنا; وملئه is conjoined to فرعون; and بآياتنا is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "bearing our nine signs", which will be stated explicitly in Sūrat al-Isrāʾ, namely His saying the Exalted: «ولقد آتينا موسى تسع آيات بينات» (and We gave Mūsā nine clear signs). Eight of them have already been mentioned in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: two in His saying «فألقى موسى عصاه» (so Mūsā cast down his staff) and His saying «ونزع يده» (and he drew out his hand); one in His saying «ولقد أخذنا آل فرعون بالسنين» (and We seized the people of Pharaoh with years of drought); and five in His saying «فأرسلنا عليهم الطوفان» (so We sent upon them the flood). The ninth will come in this sūra in His saying «ربنا اطمس على أموالهم» (our Lord, obliterate their wealth), i.e. transform it into stones, as will come in its place.
(فَاسْتَكْبَرُوا وَكانُوا قَوْماً مُجْرِمِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; استكبروا is a verb and an agent; كانوا: kāna and its noun; قوما is its khabar; and مجرمين is an adjective. (فَلَمَّا جاءَهُمُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ عِنْدِنا) The fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is temporal or a connector; the clause جاءهم is added (muḍāf) [to it], or has no position; الحق is the agent; and من عندنا is attached to جاءهم. (قالُوا: إِنَّ هذا لَسِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ) The clause قالوا has no position; inna and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); سحر is the khabar of إن; and مبين is an adjective. (قالَ مُوسى: أَتَقُولُونَ لِلْحَقِّ لَمَّا جاءَكُمْ أَسِحْرٌ هذا وَلا يُفْلِحُ السَّاحِرُونَ) قال موسى is a verb and an agent; the hamza is interrogative; تقولون is an imperfect verb and an agent; للحق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تقولون; لما is temporal and the clause جاءكم is added to it; أسحر: the hamza is for denunciatory, reproachful interrogation; سحر is a fronted khabar and هذا a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the sentence is the content of the saying; ولا: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and لا is negative; يفلح الساحرون is an imperfect verb and an agent, and the clause is circumstantial. (قالُوا أَجِئْتَنا لِتَلْفِتَنا عَمَّا وَجَدْنا عَلَيْهِ آباءَنا) قالوا is a verb and an agent; the hamza is for explanatory interrogation (istifhām bayānī) in which the stubborn obstinate person exhausts his collapsing arguments in order to justify his persistence in contentiousness, dissimulation and obstinacy; the clause أجئتنا is the content of the saying, a verb, an agent and a direct object; لتلفتنا: the lām is for reason, and تلفت is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied أن after the lām of reason; عما is attached to تلفتنا; the clause وجدنا is a ṣila; عليه is attached to an omitted ḥāl, its implied form being "devoted"; and آباءنا is a direct object. (وَتَكُونَ لَكُمَا الْكِبْرِياءُ فِي الْأَرْضِ) The wāw is a conjunction; تكون is an imperfect defective verb; ولكما is its fronted khabar; الكبرياء is its delayed noun; and في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "extending". الكبرياء is a maṣdar on the pattern فعلياء, and its meaning is greatness; it was also said to mean kingship, because kings are described by pride, and hence the king is called a tyrant (jabbār). Bashshār ibn Burd said:
إذا الملك الجبار صعّر خده ... مشينا إليه بالسيوف نعاتبه
(When the tyrant king turns his cheek away in pride, we walk to him with swords to reproach him.)
They described them with arrogance and haughtiness, and for that reason Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt described Muṣʿab in his saying:
ملكه ملك رأفة ليس فيه ... جبروت منه ولا كبرياء
(His kingship is a kingship of compassion; in it is no tyranny from him, nor pride.)
negating what kings are upon of that.
(وَما نَحْنُ لَكُما بِمُؤْمِنِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is Hijāzī (operating like ليس) and نحن is its noun; بمؤمنين: the bāʾ is redundant and مؤمنين is the khabar of ما in position.
[Translator's note: "Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt" is my expansion of the source's "ابن الرقيات"; the text gives only the shortened name.]

* Benefits:
Ibn Hishām said, in the course of his discussion of the omission of the object: "Among its rare cases is the omission of the thing said while the saying remains, as in: قال موسى: أتقولون للحق لما جاءكم, i.e. 'it is magic', by the evidence of أسحر هذا."
There is a good deal of obscurity in this statement, and al-Dasūqī followed it up, saying: "What the author mentioned is one of the possibilities mentioned in al-Kashshāf, and its wording is: 'If you say: they were certain, by their saying «إن هذا لسحر مبين», that it was magic; so how was it said to them "Do you say: is this magic?" I say: there are several possibilities. That the meaning of His saying «أتقولون للحق» is: do you find fault with it and slander it, when you ought to submit to it and magnify it, from their saying "so-and-so fears the slander (al-qāla)", and "the people were disputing (tqāwul)" when some say to others what harms them; and like the saying here is the mention (dhikr) in his saying 'we heard a young man mention them', then he said 'is this magic?', so he denied what they said in finding fault with it and slandering it. And that the object of أتقولون is omitted, namely what is indicated by their saying «إن هذا لسحر مبين», as though it was said: "Do you say what you say?", meaning their saying 'this is clear magic'; then it was said 'is this magic?' And that the clause 'is this magic? and the magicians do not prosper' is a quotation of their speech, as though they said: "Have you two come with magic by which you seek success?"' End of what al-Zamakhsharī said." Al-Dasūqī handled it in a way that spoiled it, and so we preferred to quote what al-Zamakhsharī said verbatim from al-Kashshāf; even so it is not free of obscurity. Its clarification: the saying in the first view is a metonymy for fault-finding and so does not require an object; in the second it requires an object. What we hold is that Ibn Hishām's question is not valid, and that al-Zamakhsharī's objection and his effort to answer it are not valid either, and for that reason we passed over all of this in the i'rab. Better than all of it is the wording of Abū al-Suʿūd, which is: "Mūsā said, that is, he said three sentences. The first: «أتقولون للحق لما جاءكم»; the second: «أسحر هذا»; the third: «ولا يفلح الساحرون». His saying «للحق» means concerning it and for its sake; and his saying «لما جاءكم» means at the time of its coming to you from the very beginning, without reflection or consideration, which is contrary to the said saying. And «إنه لسحر» is the content of the saying, omitted because what precedes it indicates it, and as an indication that he does not utter it. And «أسحر هذا» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar and is a denunciatory interrogation, resumptive, from his side (peace be upon him), as a denial of their saying, and a reproach after reproach and a charge of ignorance after ignorance. And «ولا يفلح الساحرون» is a circumstantial clause from the pronoun of those addressed, and the connector is the wāw without a pronoun, as in the saying of one who said: 'The winter came and I own no provision', i.e. 'Do you say of the truth that it is magic, when its doer does not prosper', that is, he neither attains what he seeks nor escapes what he dislikes; so how could it issue from one like me, among those supported by the Almighty, the Wise?'"
[Translator's note: some of the quoted Kashshāf passage is obscure in the source (the clause "من قولهم فلان يخاف القالة" and the verse «سمعنا فتى يذكرهم»); I have translated it as printed. The words "Ibn Hishām's" statement is quoted from Mughnī al-Labīb.]

dervis-irab:79-82.t:
* I'rab:
(وَقالَ فِرْعَوْنُ ائْتُونِي بِكُلِّ ساحِرٍ عَلِيمٍ) The wāw is a conjunction, so that the parts of the story run in sequence; قال فرعون is a verb and an agent; ائتوني is an imperative verb, an agent and a direct object; بكل is attached to ائتوني; ساحر is a muḍāf ilayhi; and عليم is an adjective. (فَلَمَّا جاءَ السَّحَرَةُ قالَ لَهُمْ مُوسى أَلْقُوا ما أَنْتُمْ مُلْقُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction to an omitted clause, i.e. "so they brought the magicians"; the clause قال لهم موسى has no position; ألقوا is an imperative verb and an agent; ما is a relative noun, a direct object; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ملقون a khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; and the clause ألقوا is the content of the saying. (فَلَمَّا أَلْقَوْا قالَ مُوسى ما جِئْتُمْ بِهِ السِّحْرُ) ما is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ; the clause جئتم به is a ṣila; and السحر is the khabar. In one reading, آلسحر with two hamzas, a hamza of interrogation and the hamza of the article; then ما is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and جئتم به is the khabar, the implied form being "what is it that you brought?", as though it were an interrogation of denial and belittlement of what they brought; and السحر is a substitute (badal) for the interrogative noun, which is why its particle is repeated with it; or السحر is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "is it magic?". (إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَيُبْطِلُهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُصْلِحُ عَمَلَ الْمُفْسِدِينَ) inna and its noun, and the clause سيبطله is its khabar; and inna and its noun, and the clause لا يصلح is its khabar; the second إن is for giving a reason; and عمل المفسدين is a direct object. (وَيُحِقُّ اللَّهُ الْحَقَّ بِكَلِماتِهِ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُجْرِمُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; يحق الله is a verb and an agent; الحق is a direct object; بكلماته is attached to يحق; ولو: the wāw is circumstantial and لو is connective (waṣliyya); كره المجرمون is a verb and an agent.

dervis-irab:83-86.t:
* I'rab:
(فَما آمَنَ لِمُوسى إِلَّا ذُرِّيَّةٌ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction to an omitted clause understood from the context and from what is detailed in other places, i.e. "so he cast down his staff and lo, it swallowed what they fabricated"; ما is negative; آمن is a past verb; لموسى is attached to it; إلا is a particle of restriction; ذرية is the agent; and من قومه is an adjective. (عَلى خَوْفٍ مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَائِهِمْ أَنْ يَفْتِنَهُمْ) على here means "with" (maʿa), and it with its genitive noun is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); من فرعون is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خوف; وملئهم is conjoined to فرعون. He used the plural pronoun for it only because فرعون here means the people of Pharaoh, as one says Rabīʿa and Muḍar; or because he has companions who act at his command. أن يفتنهم: أن and what is in its domain are a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) for فرعون, i.e. "out of fear of the persecution of Pharaoh", or an object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi) after the omission of the lām. (وَإِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ لَعالٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَإِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الْمُسْرِفِينَ) The wāw is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya), and this clause and the one after it are an appended parenthesis (iʿtirāḍ tadhyīlī); inna and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); عال is the khabar of إن, nominative, its sign being the implied ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عال; وإنه: the wāw is also parenthetical; inna and its noun; the shifted lām; and من المسرفين is the khabar of إن. (وَقالَ مُوسى: يا قَوْمِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ آمَنْتُمْ بِاللَّهِ فَعَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلُوا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُسْلِمِينَ) يا قوم: يا is a vocative particle and قوم is the one addressed, added to the yāʾ of the first person, whose ruling has already been given; we add here that the omission of the yāʾ is stronger than retaining it, because of the strength of the vocative for change. إن is conditional; كنتم is in the position of the jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the tāʾ being the noun of كان, and the clause آمنتم its khabar; بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنتم; فعليه:
the fāʾ is a connector of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and عليه is attached to توكلوا; توكلوا is an imperative verb and an agent; إن is conditional; كنتم مسلمين: kāna, its noun and its khabar; and the apodosis is omitted, the clause being repeated for emphasis. The verification of making a ruling dependent on two conditions will come in the Benefits section. (فَقالُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْنا) The fāʾ is for conjunction; قالوا is a verb and an agent; على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to توكلنا; and توكلنا is a verb and an agent. (رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا فِتْنَةً لِلْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ) ربنا is a muḍāf vocative whose particle is omitted; لا is prohibitive; تجعلنا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, and نا is a first direct object; فتنة is a second direct object; للقوم is an adjective; and الظالمين is an adjective of قوم. (وَنَجِّنا بِرَحْمَتِكَ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الْكافِرِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; نج is an imperative verb, indeclinable with the omission of the weak letter; نا is a direct object; برحمتك is attached to an omitted ḥāl; من القوم is attached to نجنا; and الكافرين is an adjective of قوم.

* Benefits:
Whenever two conditions are not ordered in existence, the second condition is a condition in the first, and for that reason it is not obligatory to put it first. On this the jurists built a curious ruling, namely that a man says to his wife: "If you enter the house, you are divorced, if you speak to Zayd." The whole of his saying "if you enter the house you are divorced" is conditioned by his saying "if you speak to Zayd", and the conditioned comes after the condition. That requires that what is later in wording be earlier in meaning, and that what is earlier in wording be later in meaning; it is as though he said to his wife: "As soon as you speak to Zayd, if you enter the house you are divorced." So if this suspended event occurred before "if you speak to Zayd", the divorce does not take effect. In the verse we are concerned with, His saying: «إن كنتم آمنتم بالله فعليه توكلوا إن كنتم مسلمين» requires that their being Muslims be a condition for their becoming addressed by His saying «إن كنتم آمنتم بالله فعليه توكلوا»; it is as though He, the Exalted, says to the Muslim in the state of his submission: "If you are among those who believe in Allah, then put your trust in Allah." And so it is, because Islam is an expression for submission (istislām), which is yielding to Allah's obligations and abandoning rebellion, while faith (īmān) is an expression for the heart's knowledge that the Necessary Existent in Himself is one and that all else is originated, under His governance and subjugation. When these two states occur, then the servant entrusts all his affairs to Allah the Exalted, and the light of trust in Allah arises in the heart.

dervis-irab:87-89.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَبَوَّءا): تبوّأ المكان means he took it as a dwelling (mabāʾa), like your saying توطنه when he took it as a homeland; and بوأت له بيتا, i.e. I made it a dwelling for him. Abū ʿAlī said: تبوأ is a verb that takes two objects.
(اطْمِسْ): الطمس is the removal of the trace of a thing by erasure; طمست الريح آثار الديار (the wind effaced the traces of the abodes). الطمس is change toward obliteration and effacement. Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr said:
من كل نضّاخة الذّفرى إذا عرقت ... عرضتها طامس الأعلام مجهول
(Of every she-camel gushing at the back of the ear when she sweats, whose way she crosses is one with obliterated landmarks, unknown.)

* I'rab:
