(وَأَوْحَيْنا إِلى مُوسى وَأَخِيهِ أَنْ تَبَوَّءا لِقَوْمِكُما بِمِصْرَ بُيُوتاً) The wāw is resumptive; أوحينا is a verb and an agent; إلى موسى is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوحينا; وأخيه is conjoined to موسى. أن may be explicative (mufassira), since what has the meaning of "saying" without its letters precedes it, namely revelation (īḥāʾ); and it may be maṣdarī in its normal sense, with what follows it in the position of the accusative as the object of أوحينا, i.e. "We revealed to them the taking up of dwellings". ولقومكما is attached to تبوءا, regarded as a second object; بمصر is a ḥāl; بيوتا is the object of تبوءا; and Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that it be attached to تبوءا. (وَاجْعَلُوا بُيُوتَكُمْ قِبْلَةً وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) واجعلوا is conjoined to تبوءا; بيوتكم is the first object of اجعلوا and قبلة its second object; وأقيموا الصلاة is conjoined, being an imperative verb, an agent and a direct object; وبشر المؤمنين is likewise conjoined. The secret of the variation of address will come in the Rhetoric section. (وَقالَ مُوسى رَبَّنا إِنَّكَ آتَيْتَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَأَهُ زِينَةً وَأَمْوالًا فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا) قال موسى is a verb and an agent; ربنا is a muḍāf vocative whose particle is omitted; inna and its noun, and the clause آتيت is the khabar of إن; فرعون is a direct object; وملأه is conjoined to فرعون; زينة is a second direct object; وأموالا is conjoined to زينة; and في الحياة الدنيا is an adjective of زينة. (رَبَّنا لِيُضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِكَ) ربنا is a muḍāf vocative, repeated for emphasis; the lām is the lām of outcome and consequence (ṣayrūra wa-ʿāqiba), i.e. "You gave them the mentioned blessings that they might give thanks for them and follow Your path, but the consequence of their affair was that they disbelieved in them and went astray from Your path". It is also possible that it is the lām of reason, the meaning being that You gave them what You gave by way of gradual drawing on (istidrāj), so the giving was for this reason. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said: it is the lām of supplication against them, that they remain in the error they are in. وعن سبيلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يضلوا. (رَبَّنَا اطْمِسْ عَلى أَمْوالِهِمْ وَاشْدُدْ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ) اطمس is an imperative verb whose agent is "you"; على قلوبهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اطمس [sic]; and واشدد على قلوبهم is conjoined to اطمس على أموالهم. (فَلا يُؤْمِنُوا حَتَّى يَرَوُا الْعَذابَ الْأَلِيمَ) يؤمنوا admits the accusative and the jussive. The accusative is by an implied أن after the fāʾ of causation, a conjunction; or it is conjoined to His saying ليضلوا, "so that they do not believe", and al-Mubarrad chose it; on this His saying «ربنا اطمس على أموالهم واشدد على قلوبهم» is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ). The jussive is on the sense of supplication against them, on the basis that the لا which the grammarians call prohibitive is, in relation to Allah the Exalted, the lām of supplication; and like it is the verse of al-Aʿshā:
فلا ينبسط من بين عينيك ما انزوى ... ولا تلقني إلا وأنفك راغم
(May what is drawn together between your eyes never relax, and may you never meet me except with your nose in the dust.)
حتى is a particle of limit and governing the genitive; يروا is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied أن after حتى, and the wāw is the agent; العذاب is a direct object; and الأليم is an adjective. (قالَ قَدْ أُجِيبَتْ دَعْوَتُكُما) The clause قد أجيبت is the content of the saying, and دعوتكما is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
(فَاسْتَقِيما وَلا تَتَّبِعانِّ سَبِيلَ الَّذِينَ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) The fāʾ is the eloquent (faṣīḥa) fāʾ; استقيما is an imperative verb and the alif is the agent; ولا تتبعان: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is prohibitive; تتبعان is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, its sign being the omission of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the agent; the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis, and it takes kasra because it occurs after the alif of the dual. Ḥafṣ read تتبعان with a lightened kasra-vowelled nūn and a doubled tāʾ [sic]; so it is possible that لا is negative, or prohibitive. If it is negative, the nūn is the nūn of the nominative and the clause is nominal, i.e. "and you two do not follow", or it is a pure resumptive report with no connection to what follows; and if it is prohibitive, the nūn is for emphasis, the light one. سبيل is a direct object; الذين is a muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause لا يعلمون is a ṣila.
[Translator's note: the description of Ḥafṣ's reading is given in the source in this form (تتبعان with a doubled tāʾ and a lightened nūn); I have translated it as printed.]

* Rhetoric:
Variation in address. He, glorified is He, varied His address to them: first the dual, then the plural, then the singular at the end. The secret in that is that Mūsā and Hārūn were addressed to take up dwellings for their two peoples and choose them for worship; then the address was made general to them and their people in taking mosques for prayer in them, because that is an obligation upon the community at large; then finally Mūsā was singled out for the glad tidings, which is the loftiest purpose, in magnification of it and of the one given the tidings.

dervis-irab:41-44.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ كَذَّبُوكَ فَقُلْ لِي عَمَلِي وَلَكُمْ عَمَلُكُمْ): The wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; كذبوك is a verb, agent and direct object, in the position of the jussive as the protasis; فقل: the فاء is the linking one, because what follows it is a clause of request; قل is an imperative verb; لي is a fronted khabar; عملي is a delayed mubtadaʾ; ولكم عملكم is conjoined; and the clause لي عملي is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying. (أَنْتُمْ بَرِيئُونَ مِمَّا أَعْمَلُ): أنتم is a mubtadaʾ; بريئون is the khabar; مما is attached to بريئون; and the clause أعمل is the ṣila of the relative. (وَأَنَا بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ): conjoined to what has gone before, and the i'rab is plain. (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ): The wāw is a conjunction; منهم is a fronted khabar; من is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and يستمعون is an adjective of من if it is an indefinite described noun, that is, "people who listen", and a ṣila if it is a relative; and he returned the pronoun in the plural, regarding the meaning of من, though more often its wording is regarded, as in His saying «ومنهم من ينظر إليك»; reference to this has been made many times. إليك is attached to يستمعون. (أَفَأَنْتَ تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ وَلَوْ كانُوا لا يَعْقِلُونَ): The hamza is for denying interrogation; the فاء is a conjunction of immediate sequence, and in it are the two well-known aspects, of regarding an omission of the one conjoined to, or regarding fronting and delaying, both of which have been indicated before; the wāw is a conjunction; لو and what attaches to it; كانوا is kāna and its noun; and the clause لا يعقلون is its khabar. al-Zajjāj said: its meaning is "even if they were ignorant", in addition to deafness; when the removal of hearing and the removal of intellect come together, the matter is complete and the human being has lost all human characteristics. (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْكَ): conjoined to the preceding one and its like, but here he carried the pronoun on the wording of من; and the difference between the two places is that the listeners are mostly a group, while the one looking is mostly a single person. (أَفَأَنْتَ تَهْدِي الْعُمْيَ وَلَوْ كانُوا لا يُبْصِرُونَ): conjoined to what has gone before, and the meaning is "even if to lack of sight were added lack of insight". The apodosis of لو in the two clauses is omitted, on the indication of His saying أفأنت تسمع الصم and His saying أفأنت تهدي العمي; and each of them is conjoined to an implied clause opposed to it, and both are in the position of the ḥāl from the object of the preceding verb, that is: "Will you make the deaf hear, if they were to use reason, and if they were not to use reason? Will you guide the blind, if they were to see and if they were not to see?", that is, you do not make them hear and you do not guide them in any case. More on this simile will come in the section on Rhetoric. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَظْلِمُ النَّاسَ شَيْئاً): إن is a particle resembling the verb; الله is its noun; the clause لا يظلم is its khabar; الناس is a direct object; and شيئا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, that is, "any bit of wrong", and it is possible that it be a second object of يظلم, in the sense "He does not diminish anything of people's deeds".
(وَلكِنَّ النَّاسَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ): The wāw is ḥāl; لكن is a particle of istidrāk and of governing the accusative; الناس is its noun; أنفسهم is a fronted direct object of يظلمون; and the clause يظلمون is the khabar of لكن.

* Rhetoric:
1- The representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya):
In His saying the Exalted «ومنهم من يستمعون إليك» to the end of the verse there is a representational metaphor, and it has already been said that the representational metaphor is a composition used for other than what it was set for, on account of a relation of resemblance. He likened them, in their not being guided, to the deaf and the blind; indeed they are worse, for «it is not the eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts»; and because the deaf who has intellect may sometimes use physiognomy to draw inference, and the blind who has insight in his heart may guess and surmise. The thing likened to has come composite because the thing likened is also composite; and had he resorted to simile, the artistic effect would have dwindled and would not have had that value we notice in the metaphor, because the metaphor, though built on observation, yet its composition induces us to forget the simile and calls us to imagine a new image; and in terms of wording, as you see in the verse, it leaves the dual expression, that is, the likened and the likened to, and uses the single expression, which claims that there is only one thing we are speaking of; and invention keeps its effect in tying a successful metaphor, and in this field the genius of artists and creators shines forth.
Moreover, Abū al-Ṭayyib looked up to the sky of this eloquence with his saying:
وإذا خفيت على الغبي فعاذر ... أن لا تراني مقلة عمياء
(If I am hidden from the dullard, he is excused that a blind eyeball does not see me.)
He means that if his place is hidden from the dullard, that is, the ignorant who knows nothing and did not know my worth and did not acknowledge my merit, I excuse him, because the ignorant is like the blind, and the blind eyeball, if it does not see, has its excuse in its blindness; likewise the ignorant who is ignorant of me and of my worth. And before al-Mutanabbī it was said:
وقد بهرت فما أخفى على أحد ... إلا على أكمه لا يعرف القمرا
(I have dazzled, so I am hidden from no one, except from one born blind who does not know the moon.)

2- Refinement (al-tahdhīb):
In these preceding verses there is a badīʿ art called the art of refinement, on which the scholars of this art have dwelt at length, and it can be summarised as a description that covers every chosen speech, namely the repeated looking into speech after composing it, and the close thought in refining and polishing it, whether verse or prose, and uncovering what is difficult of its abstruse meanings and rare of its i'rab, and casting off what distances itself from places of delicacy, of harsh wording and a coarse, jarring word. Abū Tammām expressed it in his testament to al-Buḥturī. It is reported from Abū ʿUbāda [Translator's note: al-Buḥturī is elsewhere known as Abū ʿUbāda; the text then has Abū Tammām address him as "Abū ʿUbayda", as written] that he said: "In my youth I sought poetry and went back in it to a sound nature, and I had not yet found for it an easy approach and ways of improvisation, until I went to Abū Tammām and attached myself to him. The first thing he said to me was: O Abū ʿUbayda, choose your times when you are of few cares and empty of griefs, and know that the custom regarding times, when a person sets out to compose something or memorise it, is that he choose the hour before dawn; and do not make verse or prose in a state of weariness, for much of it is little. Thoughts are springs: if you are gentle with them they gather, and if you are rough with them they run dry. Hum the poetry at the time of making it, for it helps. A poet may imagine excellent poetry and manage it one time and not another. Beware of obscuring the meanings, and place the noble meaning in a gentle wording so that neither spoils the other. Whenever poetry disobeys you, leave it, and whenever it obeys you, return to it. Give your mind rest when it is tired, and work on the meanings you love most and on all that suits your nature, for souls give out of desire and do not give out of compulsion. Make the verses scattered, as the mind provides, then string them together at the end, and secure the opening, the transition and the close, for that is the hardest part of the poem. And distinguish with your thought the landing-place of the message and the pouring-point of the poem, for it will be easier for you. Compose it first and refine it last."

Refinement in the verse:
As for the verse we are examining, it is His saying the Exalted «ومنهم من يستمعون إليك أفأنت تسمع الصم ولو كانوا لا يعقلون، ومنهم من ينظر إليك أفأنت تهدي العمي ولو كانوا لا يبصرون». One might say: what is the benefit of the two closing clauses, when what precedes them has made them unnecessary? It is answered that in the speech there is fronting and delaying, knowledge of which removes the question, namely that it be said «ومنهم من ينظر إليك ولو كانوا لا يبصرون أفأنت تهدي العمي», and the other likewise. Against this comes the saying of one who says: what calls for setting the speech on fronting and delaying, which is one of the causes of obscurity? I say: what calls for it is aiming to bring the clause-endings alike with what comes before and after them of the rhymed endings. For before it is: «وإن كذبوك فقل لي عملي ولكم عملكم أنتم بريئون مما أعمل وأنا بريء مما تعملون», and after it: «إن الله لا يظلم الناس شيئا ولكن الناس أنفسهم كانوا يظلمون». [Translator's note: the source quotes the last verse with «كانوا يظلمون», while the Qur'an reads «يظلمون»; translated as written.] Most of the rhymed endings of the sūra are of this measure and rhyme.

dervis-irab:45-47.t:
* I'rab:
(وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ كَأَنْ لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إِلَّا ساعَةً مِنَ النَّهارِ): The adverb is attached to يتعارفون according to the soundest views; the clause يحشرهم is a genitive complement of it; كأن is the lightened form of the heavy, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter; the clause لم يلبثوا is the khabar of كأن; the clause كأن لم يلبثوا is a ḥāl from the هاء in يحشرهم; إلا is a particle of restriction; ساعة is an adverb attached to يلبثوا; and من النهار is an adjective of ساعة. (يَتَعارَفُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ): The clause is a ḥāl from the wāw in يلبثوا, so it is an interwoven ḥāl, or from the pronoun in يحشرهم, so it is a successive ḥāl; بينهم is an adverb attached to يتعارفون. The meaning after this i'rab is that the creatures will know one another at that time as they were in the world, as if they had stayed in the world only an hour of the day; then recognition will be cut off when they behold the punishment and disown one another. There are other analyses that the space is too narrow to take in, and what we have given is the closest of them. (قَدْ خَسِرَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِلِقاءِ اللَّهِ وَما كانُوا مُهْتَدِينَ): قد is a particle of affirmation; خسر الذين is a verb and agent; the clause كذبوا is a ṣila; بلقاء الله, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to كذبوا; the clause قد خسر is resumptive; the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; كان with its noun; and مهتدين is its khabar; and it is conjoined to قد خسر or to the ṣila of الذين, because whoever denies Allah is not guided. (وَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ الَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ): إن is conditional and ما redundant; نرينك is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "We"; the kāf is a direct object; بعض is a second object; الذي is a muḍāf ilayhi; the clause نعدهم is a ṣila; أو is a particle of conjunction; and نتوفينك is conjoined to نرينك. (فَإِلَيْنا مَرْجِعُهُمْ ثُمَّ اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ عَلى ما يَفْعَلُونَ): The فاء is the linking one; إلينا is a fronted khabar; مرجعهم is a delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the apodosis; ثم is a conjunction, not of temporal order but of the order of reports; الله is a mubtadaʾ and شهيد the khabar; على ما يفعلون is attached to شهيد; and the clause يفعلون is a ṣila. (وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَسُولٌ): لكل is a fronted khabar; أمة is a muḍāf ilayhi of كل; and رسول is a delayed mubtadaʾ. (فَإِذا جاءَ رَسُولُهُمْ قُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْقِسْطِ وَهُمْ لا يُظْلَمُونَ): The فاء is conjoined to the description of رسول, that is, "he is sent to them, and when..."; إذا is an adverb of the future; the clause جاء رسولهم is a genitive complement of it; the clause قضي has no grammatical position; بينهم is an adverb attached to قضي; بالقسط is a ḥāl from the nāʾib fāʿil of قضي; the wāw in وهم is a conjunction or ḥāl; هم is a mubtadaʾ; and the clause لا يظلمون is the khabar.

dervis-irab:48-52.t:
* I'rab:
(وَيَقُولُونَ مَتى هذَا الْوَعْدُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): The wāw is resumptive; يقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the persistence of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; متى is an interrogative about time, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; هذا is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and الوعد is a badal. This expression is a sort of finding improbable what they were promised of punishment. إن is conditional; كنتم is the protasis, the tāʾ being the noun of كان; صادقين is its khabar; and the apodosis is omitted, that is, "then when is this promise?" (قُلْ لا أَمْلِكُ لِنَفْسِي ضَرًّا وَلا نَفْعاً إِلَّا ما شاءَ اللَّهُ): The clause لا أملك is the content of the saying; لنفسي is attached to أملك; ضرا is a direct object; ولا نفعا is conjoined to ضرا; إلا is a particle of exception or restriction, given the presence of the negation; ما is a relative noun, the excepted. It was said that the exception is connected, and it was said disconnected; and if «إلا» is restriction, then ما is a badal of ضرا and نفعا; and the clause شاء الله is a ṣila. (لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلٌ): a completion of the content of the saying; لكل is a fronted khabar; أمة is a muḍāf ilayhi; and أجل is a delayed mubtadaʾ. (إِذا جاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ فَلا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ ساعَةً وَلا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ): إذا is an adverb of the future; the clause جاء is a genitive complement of it; أجلهم is the agent of جاء; the فاء is the linking one; لا is negative; the clause يستأخرون has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of إذا; ساعة is an adverb attached to يستأخرون; and لا يستقدمون is conjoined to فلا يستأخرون. (قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَتاكُمْ عَذابُهُ بَياتاً أَوْ نَهاراً): قل is an imperative verb whose agent is "you", that is, Muḥammad; the clause أرأيتم is the content of the saying. The discussion of أرأيتم has gone before, in sūrat al-Anʿām, and we said there that the Arabs include in أرأيت the meaning of "tell me", and that it then takes two objects, the second of which is mostly an interrogative clause, which together with what precedes it forms a mubtadaʾ and khabar; the Arabs say أرأيت زيد ما صنع, and the meaning is "tell me about Zayd, what he did". Having mentioned this, the first object of أرأيتم here is omitted, and the conditional clause cannot take its place. The matter is of the chapter of tanāzuʿ (competition between two operators), the competition of أرأيتم and أتاكم in His saying عذابه, and giving the operation to the second is the preferred view; so when it was made to operate, it was omitted from the first. The meaning is: "Say to them, O Muḥammad, tell me about the punishment of Allah, if it comes to you, what part of it do you wish to hasten?", and there is no part of the punishment that a sensible person would hasten, because the punishment is all bitter in taste, evil in outcome, necessitating aversion from it. إن is conditional; أتاكم is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the apodosis is the interrogative clause with an implied فاء, in the nominal clause; بياتا is accusative as an adverb attached to أتاكم; and أو نهارا is conjoined to it. (ماذا يَسْتَعْجِلُ مِنْهُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ): ما may be in the position of the nominative, namely when ذا is in the sense of الذي, the meaning being "what is it that the criminals hasten of it?", so ما is a mubtadaʾ and الذي its khabar; and it may be in the position of the accusative, namely when you make ما and ذا one noun, the meaning being "what thing do the criminals hasten of it?", so it is the object of يستعجل and المجرمون is the agent of يستعجل. (أَثُمَّ إِذا ما وَقَعَ آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ آلْآنَ وَقَدْ كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ): أثم: the hamza is for denying interrogation and ثم is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb of the future; ما is redundant; the clause وقع is in the position of the genitive by annexation to it; the clause آمنتم به is a ṣila; the adverb is attached to آمنتم; آلآن: the hamza is for denying interrogation, and الآن is an adverb attached to an omitted element understood from the context, its implied form being "Do you believe in it now?"; the wāw is ḥāl; قد is a particle of affirmation; كنتم is kāna and its noun; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تستعجلون; and the clause تستعجلون is the khabar of كنتم. (ثُمَّ قِيلَ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا ذُوقُوا عَذابَ الْخُلْدِ هَلْ تُجْزَوْنَ إِلَّا بِما كُنْتُمْ تَكْسِبُونَ): ثم is a conjunction; قيل is a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil is latent; للذين is attached to قيل; the clause ظلموا is a ṣila; the clause ذوقوا is the content of the saying; عذاب is a direct object; الخلد is a muḍāf ilayhi; هل is a particle of interrogation; تجزون is an imperfect verb and nāʾib fāʿil; إلا is a particle of restriction; بما is attached to تجزون; the clause كنتم is a ṣila; and the clause تكسبون is the khabar of كنتم.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying: بياتا ونهارا and ضرا ونفعا there is ṭibāq (antithesis) which, when repeated, is called muqābala (balancing), and an istiʿāra makniyya (implicit metaphor) in His saying ذوقوا عذاب الخلد; reference to all that has already been made.

dervis-irab:53-56.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الاستنباء): the request for the nabaʾ, which is the report.
(الافتداء): putting a thing in place of another to ward off something disliked by it. One says فداه يفديه فدية وفداء and افتداه and فاداه مفاداة. افتدى may be transitive or intransitive; if it is the compliant form (muṭāwiʿ) of a transitive verb it is intransitive, as you say فديته فافتدى; and if it is not compliant, it is in the sense of فدى and takes one object. The verb here admits of both aspects; if we make it transitive, its object is omitted, the implied form being "she would ransom herself with it".
(أَسَرُّوا النَّدامَةَ): It was said that أسر is among the ḍidd words (words with opposite senses), used in the sense of "made manifest" and in the sense of "concealed", which is the well-known one in the language; in the verse it admits of both aspects.

* I'rab:
(وَيَسْتَنْبِئُونَكَ أَحَقٌّ هُوَ قُلْ إِي وَرَبِّي): ويستنبئونك is an imperfect verb, agent and direct object; أحق: the hamza is for denying interrogation, tinged with mockery; حق is a fronted khabar and هو a delayed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as an object of يستنبئونك. It was also said that the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of يقولون, with يستنبئونك being transitive to one; for the origin of استنبأ is that it takes two objects, one of them with «عن»; you say استنبأت زيدا عن عمرو, that is, I asked him to inform me about ʿAmr. قل is an imperative verb; إي is a particle of reply, and the particles of reply will be treated in the section on Benefits; the wāw in وربي is for oath, and ربي is genitive by the wāw of oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted verb of the oath. (إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ وَما أَنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ): إن with its noun and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the wāw is a conjunction upon the answer of the oath, or resumptive, conveyed to explain that they will not be free from Allah's punishment in any way; ما is Ḥijāzī; أنتم is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; and معجزين is its khabar, in the position of the accusative in place, and genitive by the redundant bāʾ in wording. (وَلَوْ أَنَّ لِكُلِّ نَفْسٍ ظَلَمَتْ ما فِي الْأَرْضِ لَافْتَدَتْ بِهِ): The wāw is resumptive; لو is the conditional of prevention, as is common for it; أن is a particle resembling the verb; لكل is the fronted khabar of أن; نفس is a muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ظلمت is an adjective of نفس; ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative, the noun of أن; and أن and what is within its scope is the agent of an omitted verb, that is, "if that were established"; في الأرض is the ṣila of ما; the lām falls in the apodosis of لو; and افتدت به is a verbal clause with no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (وَأَسَرُّوا النَّدامَةَ لَمَّا رَأَوُا الْعَذابَ): The wāw is a conjunction; أسروا الندامة is a verb, agent and direct object; لما is a linking particle or temporal; the clause رأوا is a genitive complement of it, or a ṣila; the wāw is the agent and العذاب a direct object. The meaning is that they were stunned and bewildered at seeing what had never crossed their minds or occurred to them, so they were folded upon anguish and guarded against the disclosure of the one who feigns fortitude, and they had no power beyond concealing regret and sorrow in their hearts. It was also said أسروا الندامة means they made it manifest, from their saying أسر الشيء وأشره when he made it manifest; this was said by Abū ʿUbayda and al-Jubbāʾī, and al-Azharī denied that it could be in the sense of making manifest and said that it is a sheer mistake, because what is in the sense of making manifest is with the three-dotted shīn. (وَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْقِسْطِ وَهُمْ لا يُظْلَمُونَ): It is possible that the speech be resumptive and that it be conjoined; قضي is a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil is latent; بينهم is an adverb attached to قضي; بالقسط is a ḥāl; the wāw in وهم is a conjunction; and the clause لا يظلمون is the khabar. (أَلا إِنَّ لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): ألا is a word used for alerting, with which speech is opened, so it is called a particle of opening; its origin is لا, the particle of interrogation having entered upon it for affirmation and reminding, so it became an alert. إن is given kasra after ألا because what follows ألا begins anew, to alert by it to the sense of commencement; for that reason command and supplication come after it, as in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays: ألا عم صباحا أيّها الطّلل البالي ... وهل يعمن من كان في العصر الخالي (Good morning, O worn-out ruin! Does one who lived in a bygone age ever enjoy a good morning?) ولله is the fronted khabar of إن and ما its delayed noun; and في السموات والأرض is the ṣila. (أَلا إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ): ألا is an emphasis of the first ألا; the two clauses were opened with the two particles of alerting to indicate confirmation and recording of their content; إن and its noun, and حق is its khabar. (وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): The wāw is ḥāl or resumptive; لكن and its noun; and the clause لا يعلمون is its khabar. (هُوَ يُحيِي وَيُمِيتُ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ): هو is a mubtadaʾ; the clause يحيي is the khabar; the clause يميت is conjoined; and إليه, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to ترجعون.

* Benefits:
Particles of reply:
The particles of affirmation, or reply, or assent, are: نعم, بلى, أجل, جير, إي and إن. Some of them have been discussed before, and here we speak of إي and إن. As for إي, it is a particle of affirmation used only in oaths. Allah the Exalted said «قل إي وربي لتبعثن». Its hamza has kasra and the yāʾ in it has sukūn. al-Zamakhsharī said: "I heard them say إيو, joining it with the wāw of oath, and they do not pronounce it alone." Another said: "From it is the people's saying in reply إي والله and their saying «إيوه»; the wāw is for oath and the hāʾ is taken from الله." So the common people's «إيوه» is correct and open to no objection.

Particles of alerting:
They are: ها, ألا and أما. The meaning of these particles is to alert the addressee to what you are telling him. When you say هذا عبد الله منطلقا, the implied form is "look at him going off" or "pay attention to him going off"; so you alert the addressee to ʿAbd Allāh while he is going off. al-Nābigha said:
ها إنّ تا عذره إن لم تكن نفعت ... فإن صاحبها قد تاه في البلد
(Behold, this is his excuse; if it has not availed, then its owner has gone astray in the land.)
He entered ها, which is for alerting, upon إن. العذر, المعذرة and العذرى are one; and العذرة, with kasra, is like الركبة and الجلسة in the sense of "state". Another said:
تقبّل عذرتي وحبا بدهم ... يصمّ حنينها سمع المنادي
(Accept my excuse, and a gift of dark camels whose yearning deafens the hearing of the caller.)
Most often ها enters upon demonstratives and pronouns, as in your saying هذا, هذه, هأنذا, ها أنت ذا, ها هي ذه and the like. Alerting is frequent in these vague nouns only to stir the soul toward seeking a specific thing, since there is no mark of definition in their wording. The difference between ألا and أما is that أما is for the present and ألا is for the future. You say أما أن زيدا عاقل, meaning that he is intelligent in reality and not figuratively. As for the saying of the Hudhalī:
أما والذي أبكى وأضحك والذي ... أمات وأحيا والذي أمره الأمر
(By Him who makes weep and makes laugh, and who gives death and gives life, and whose command is the command!)
he entered أما upon the particle of oath, as if alerting the addressee to listen to his oath and to the verification of what is sworn upon. They sometimes drop the alif from أما and say أم والله. In the speech of Hajras ibn Kulayb: «أم وسيفي وزريه، ورمحي ونصليه، وفرسي وأذنيه، لا يدع الرجل قاتل أبيه وهو ينظر اليه» (By my sword and its two edges, by my spear and its two blades, by my horse and its two ears, a man will not leave his father's killer while he is looking at him.)

dervis-irab:90-92.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَجاوَزْنا): from جاوز المكان when he passed beyond it and left it behind him.
(فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ): In al-Mukhtār: تبعه (of the pattern ṭariba and salima) when he walked behind him, or passed by him and went on with him; so too اتّبعه, which is of the pattern iftaʿala; and أتبعه, of the pattern afʿala, when he had been ahead of him and then caught up with him. Al-Akhfash said: تبعه and أتبعه are like ردفه and أردفه. Abū ʿUbayda related from al-Kisāʾī that he said: when it is meant that he followed them with good or evil, they say it with the hamza of cutting (qaṭʿ); and when it is meant that he took them as a model and followed their trail, they say it with a doubled tāʾ and a hamzat waṣl.
(بَغْياً): البغي is seeking to lord it over others without right.
(عَدْواً): In al-Ṣiḥāḥ of al-Jawharī: عدا عدوا وعدوّا وعداء; and in al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj also عدوانا and عدوى عليه: he wronged him. And it is said: «ما عدا مما بدا» ("what has turned you from me after what has appeared from you?").
(نُنَجِّيكَ): from النجوة, which is land that the flood does not rise over; its origin is from elevation.

* I'rab:
(وَجاوَزْنا بِبَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ الْبَحْرَ) The wāw is resumptive and the sentence is resumptive, brought to explain what the affair of Pharaoh and his people came to; جاوزنا is a verb and an agent; ببني إسرائيل is attached to جاوزنا, and the bāʾ is for transitivity (taʿdiya), i.e. "We made them cross the sea"; and البحر is a direct object. (فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ وَجُنُودُهُ بَغْياً وَعَدْواً) فأتبعهم: the fāʾ is a conjunction; أتبعهم is a verb and a direct object; فرعون is the agent; وجنوده is conjoined to فرعون; بغيا is an object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi) and عدوا is conjoined to it; it is also possible that both are maṣdars in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "oppressing and transgressing". (حَتَّى إِذا أَدْرَكَهُ الْغَرَقُ قالَ آمَنْتُ أَنَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا الَّذِي آمَنَتْ بِهِ بَنُوا إِسْرائِيلَ وَأَنَا مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ) حتى is a particle of limit for his pursuit; إذا is an adverbial of the future; أدركه الغرق is a verb, a direct object and an agent, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation; the clause قال has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; the clause آمنت is the content of the saying; أن and what is in its domain are in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are the complement of آمنت; and لا إله إلا الذي has already been discussed at length; the clause آمنت is the ṣila of الذي; به is attached to آمنت; بنو إسرائيل is the agent of آمنت; وأنا: the wāw is a conjunction, أنا is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and من المسلمين is the khabar (predicate). (آلْآنَ وَقَدْ عَصَيْتَ قَبْلُ وَكُنْتَ مِنَ الْمُفْسِدِينَ) آلآن: the hamza is interrogative and الآن is an adverbial attached to an omitted word, the implied form being "Now you have believed?"; وقد: the wāw is circumstantial and قد is a particle of affirmation; عصيت is a verb and an agent; قبل is an adverbial indeclinable on ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in form but not in meaning; وكنت من المفسدين is conjoined to عصيت; كنت: kāna and its noun; and من المفسدين is its khabar. (فَالْيَوْمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ لِتَكُونَ لِمَنْ خَلْفَكَ آيَةً) The fāʾ is resumptive; اليوم is an adverbial attached to ننجيك; ببدنك is a ḥāl of the kāf, i.e. "accompanied by your body", more of which will come in the Rhetoric section; ولتكون: the lām is for reason, and تكون is accusative by an implied أن, its noun being a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; آية is its khabar; لمن خلفك is a ḥāl, and the adverbial is attached to the settling (istiqrār) that is the ṣila of the relative. (وَإِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنَ النَّاسِ عَنْ آياتِنا لَغافِلُونَ) The wāw is parenthetical, and the sentence is an appended parenthesis (iʿtirāḍ tadhyīlī) brought in after the narrative; inna and its noun; من الناس is an adjective of كثيرا; عن آياتنا is attached to غافلون; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and غافلون is the khabar of إن.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is a tawriya (double entendre) if البدن is interpreted as the coat of mail. If it is interpreted as the body, the meaning would be: "We shall save you in a state in which there is no spirit in you, you being only a body," or "with your body complete and whole, nothing diminished from it". As for interpreting البدن as the coat of mail, it is indicated by the saying of ʿAmr ibn Maʿdī Karib:
أعاذل شكتي بدني وسيفي ... وكل مقلّص سلس القياد
(O you who blame me, my armour is my coat of mail and my sword, and every lean horse easy to lead.)
Pharaoh had a coat of mail of gold by which he was recognized. In that case the tawriya in البدن is sound: in the near, apparent sense it means the body, and in the far, hidden sense it means the coat of mail, and the intended one is the far, hidden one; for Pharaoh's salvation, that is, his coming out of the sea after drowning, with his coat of mail, is a more wondrous sign than his coming out stripped. Tawriya is rare in the Qur'an and its places will come in their time; we speak of it here briefly and say:
Definition of tawriya: tawriya is that the speaker mentions a single word with two meanings: one near, apparent, not intended, and one far, hidden, which is the intended. It is divided into four types:
1- The pure tawriya (al-mujarrada), so called because it is stripped of concomitants; it too has two types:
a- The pure kind with which a concomitant of the near meaning (that by which the allusion is made) and a concomitant of the far meaning (that which is alluded to) are both mentioned, as in the saying of Mujīr al-Dīn ibn Tamīm:
وليلة بتّ أسقى في غياهبها ... راحا تسلّ شبابي من يد الهرم
ما زلت أشربها حتى نظرت إلى ... غزالة الصبح ترعى رجس الظلم
(Many a night I spent being given to drink, in its depths, a wine that draws my youth out of the hand of old age; I kept drinking it until I saw the gazelle/sun of the morning grazing on the filth of the darkness.)
For the dawn is a concomitant of the sun (ghazāla shamsiyya) and grazing is a concomitant of the wild gazelle.
b- The pure kind with which no concomitant of either meaning is mentioned, as in the saying of one of them about a year in which the month of Kānūn was mild so that the earth flowered:
كأن نيسان أهدى من ملابسه ... لشهر كانون أنواعا من الحلل
أو الغزالة من طول المدى خرفت ... فما تفرق بين الجدي والحمل
(As though Nīsān had given of its garments to the month of Kānūn all kinds of robes; or the sun, from the length of time, has grown senile and no longer distinguishes between Capricorn and Aries.)
The tawriya here is pure since the poet mentioned none of the concomitants of either meaning.
2- The ornamented tawriya (al-murashshaḥa): that in which a concomitant of the near meaning is mentioned, as in the saying of one:
يا سيدا حاز لطفا ... له البرايا عبيد
أنت الحسين ولكن ... جفاك فينا يزيد
(O master who has attained gentleness, to whom creatures are slaves: you are al-Ḥusayn, but your harshness toward us increases [Yazīd / "increases"].)
For mentioning al-Ḥusayn is a concomitant of Yazīd's being a proper name, after its possibly being the imperfect verb, which is its intended meaning, the one alluded to. And by Ibn Khaṭīb Dārayyā, about Ḥimṣ:
مدينة حمص كعبة الحسن أصبحت ... يطوف بها دان ويسعى بها قاصي
له حلة من نبتها سندسية ... تعلق في أذيال أستارها العاصي
(The city of Ḥimṣ has become a Kaʿba of beauty; the near and the far circle it and run about it; it has a robe of green brocade from its plants, and the Āṣī [Orontes / the disobedient] clings to the hems of its curtains.)
Here the mention of clinging to the hems of the Kaʿba, by way of metaphor, is an ornament for العاصي in the sense of the disobedient, as stated before. Some replied to Ibn Khaṭīb Dārayyā, saying:
مدينة حمص لم تكن قط كعبة ... يطوف بها دان ويسعى بها قاصي
ولكنها للهو والقصف حانة ... ألم تنظروها كيف جاورها العاصي
(The city of Ḥimṣ was never a Kaʿba circled by the near and run about by the far; rather it is a tavern for amusement and revelry; have you not seen how the Āṣī/the disobedient neighbours it?)
3- The explained tawriya (al-mubayyana): that in which a concomitant of the far meaning is mentioned. Among its examples is what is related that the naqīb of the Ashrāf in Baghdad loved a boy named Ṣadaqa. Ibn al-Munīr al-Ṭarābulusī took him one day and hosted him, and they sat in an upper room, when the Sharīf came to them in disguise and said to them:
يا من هم في الطبقة ... هل عندكم من شفقة؟
قد جاءكم متيّم ... يطلب منكم «صدقه»
(O you who are in the upper room, have you any compassion? A lovesick man has come to you, asking of you "charity" / "Ṣadaqa".)
Ibn al-Munīr answered him at once:
يا من أتانا سرقه ... بمهجة محترقة
جدّك يا ذا لم يجز ... أخذك منا «صدقه»
(O you who came to us stealthily, with a burning heart: your grandfather, O man, did not permit your taking "charity" from us.)
He was embarrassed and left them. The point of evidence is in the Sharīf's saying «متيم», which ornaments the alluded-to meaning in صدقة, which is the name of his beloved; the second meaning is the apparent one, namely a gift to the poor.
[Translator's note: the final sentence's relation to the verse is somewhat awkward in the source; I have translated it as printed.]
4- The prepared tawriya (al-muhayyaʾa): that in which the tawriya is not prepared in the speech except by the word before it or after it, as in the saying of al-Damāmīnī:
يا عذولي في مغن مطرب ... حرّك الأوتار لما سفرا
لم تهز العطف منه طربا ... عند ما تسمع منه وترا
(O you who blame me over a singer, a delighter, who plucked the strings when he unveiled; does it not shake your sides with delight when you hear a string/ a vengeance from him?)
The word تسمع prepared his word «وترا» for the tawriya through seeing (ruʾya), which is the far meaning; as for the near meaning, it is one of the strings of the lute.

* Benefits:
(الآن) is an adverbial of time for the moment in which you are, indeclinable on fatḥa. It is possible for the prepositions من, إلى, حتى, مذ and منذ to enter upon it, being indeclinable with them on fatḥa, and it is then in the position of the genitive.
